plus-3-reading-1.title: IELTS Practice Test Plus 3 - Reading Test 1

passages.title: Reducing electricity consumption on the Isle of Eigg
content:
Background 
The Isle of Eigg is situated off the West Coast of Scotland, and is reached by ferry from the mainland. For the island community of about a hundred residents, it has always been expensive to import products, materials and skilled labour from the mainland, and this has encouraged a culture of self-sufficiency and careful use of resources. Today, although the island now has most modern conveniences, CO2 emissions per household are 20 percent lower than the UK average, and electricity use is 50 percent lower. 
When Eigg designed its electricity grid, which was switched on in February 2008, it quickly became apparent that in order to keep the capital building costs down, it would be necessary to manage demand. This would also allow the island to generate most of its electricity from renewable sources, mainly water, wind and solar power. This goal was overseen by the Eigg Heritage Trust (EHT).

The technology 
Eigg manages electricity demand mainly by capping the instantaneous power that can be used to five kilowatts (kW) for a household and ten kW for a business. If usage goes over the limit, the electricity supply is cut off and the maintenance team must be called to come and switch it back on again. All households and businesses have energy monitors, which display current and cumulative electricity usage, and sound an alarm when consumption reaches a user-defined level, usually set a few hundred watts below the actual limit. The result is that Eigg residents have a keen sense of how much power different electrical appliances use, and are careful to minimise energy consumption. 
Demand is also managed by warning the entire island when renewable energy generation is lower than demand, and diesel generators are operating to back it up - a so-called ‘red light day’, as opposed to ‘green light days’ when there is sufficient renewable energy. Residents then take steps to temporarily reduce electricity demand further still, or postpone demand until renewable energy generation has increased. 
Energy use on the island has also been reduced through improved wall and loft insulation in homes, new boilers, solar water heating, carsharing and various small, energy-saving measures in households. New energy supplies are being developed, including sustainably harvested forests to supply wood for heating. 
Eigg Heritage Trust has installed insulation in all of its own properties at no cost to the tenants, while private properties have paid for their own insulation to be installed. The same applies for installations of solar water heating, although not all Trust properties have received this as yet. The Trust also operates a Green Grants scheme, where residents can claim 50 percent of the cost of equipment to reduce carbon emissions, up to a limit of £300. Purchases included bikes, solar water heating, secondary glazing, thicker curtains, and greenhouses to grow food locally, rather than importing it.

Environmental benefits 
Prior to the installation of the new electricity grid and renewable energy generation, most households on Eigg used diesel generators to supply electricity, resulting in significant carbon emissions. Homes were also poorly insulated and had old, inefficient oil-burning boilers, or used coal for heating. 
The work by the Eigg Heritage Trust to reduce energy use has resulted in significant reductions in carbon emissions from the island’s households and businesses. The average annual electricity use per household is just 2,160 kilowatt hours (kWh), compared to a UK average in 2008 of 4,198 kWh. Domestic carbon emissions have fallen by 47 percent, from 8.4 to 4.45 tonnes per year. This compares to average UK household emissions of 5.5 to 6 tonnes per year. The emissions should fall even further over the next few years as the supply of wood for heating increases.

Social benefits 
The completion of Eigg’s electricity grid has made a significant difference to the island’s residents, freeing them from dependence on diesel generators and providing them with a stable and affordable power supply. A reliable electricity supply has brought improvements in other areas, for example, better treatment of drinking water in some houses, and the elimination of the constant noise of diesel generators. Improved home insulation and heating has also yielded benefits, making it more affordable to keep homes at a comfortable temperature. One of the incentives for capping electricity use, rather than charging different amounts according to usage, was to make access to energy equitable. Every household has the same five kW cap, irrespective of income, so distributing the available resources equally across the island’s population.

Economic and employment benefits 
Eigg’s electricity grid supports four part-time maintenance jobs on the island, and residents have also been employed for building work to improve Trust-owned houses and other buildings. Likewise, the start of organised harvesting of wood for heating has created several forestry jobs for residents. A part-time ‘green project manager’ post has also been created. A wider economic impact has come from having a reliable and affordable electricity supply, which has enabled several new businesses to start up, including restaurants, shops, guest houses and self-catering accommodation. As Eigg has become known for cutting carbon emissions and protecting the environment, an increasing number of visitors have come to the island to learn about its work, bringing a further economic benefit to the residents.

questions.prompt: Approximately how many people live on Eigg?

explanation.step1: Question : Approximately how many people live on Eigg ? So sánh cụm từ bên câu hỏi và bài đọc, ta có: approximately = about Eigg = the island people (live on) = residents
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Background For the island community of about a hundred residents , it has always been expensive to import products, materials and skilled labour from the mainland, and this has encouraged a culture of self-sufficiency and careful use of resources."
explanation.step3: Tìm thông tin câu hỏi, trong đoạn văn Câu hỏi hỏi về how many people ( bao nhiêu người ) trên Eigg >>> dễ dàng tìm được ở phần B ackground thấy con số a hundred (100) Xác định câu trả lời Tuy nhiên ở đây nhiều bạn sẽ hơi nghi ngờ residents có = people hay ko, hay đề bẫy mình. Nếu bạn nào biết residents = dân cư = people >>> yên tâm chọn a hundred Nếu bạn nào không biết residents , có Linearthinking giúp bạn thông qua đọc cấu trúc 2 câu trong bài: For the island community of about a hundred residents , it has always been expensive to import... skilled labour from the mainland Bạn có thể dùng community = cộng đồng để đoán nghĩa residents = dân cư , hay labour = lao động để đoán tương tự Lúc này mình vẫn làm đúng, lại vừa hiểu trọn vẹn, cảm gi
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: 100/a hundred

questions.prompt: What proportion of a UK household’s electricity consumption does an Eigg household consume?

explanation.step1: Question : What proportion of a UK household’s electricity consumption does an Eigg household consume? So sánh cụm từ bên câu hỏi và bài đọc , ta có: proportion = percent UK household's electricity consumption = UK average + electricity use
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Today, although the island now has most modern conveniences, CO2 emissions per household are 20 percent lower than the UK average , and electricity use is 50 percent lower."
explanation.step3: Hiểu câu hỏi: What proportion of a UK household’s electricity consumption does an Eigg household consume? => Tỷ lệ tiêu thụ điện của Elgg household so với UK household là bao nhiêu? => Đáp án là một con số - cụ thể là tỷ lệ phần trăm => Chỉ đang nói sơ về lượng điện tiêu thụ thôi -> Chắc chắn thông tin nằm trong phần Background -> Từ đó tìm thấy 'UK' + các con số Áp dụng Linearthinking để nắm main idea: Today , although the island now has most modern conveniences , CO2 emissions per household are 20 percent lower than the UK average , and electricity use is 50 percent lower. => Thấy thông tin so sánh với UK -> Có 2 con số: 20% (C02 emissions) + 50% (electricity use) => Đối tượng của ta là mức độ tiêu thụ điện -> Answer: 50 percent/50%
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: 50 percent/50%

questions.prompt: Apart from wind and sun, where does most of Eigg’s electricity come from?

explanation.step1: Question : Apart from wind and sun , where does most of Eigg’s electricity come from ? So sánh cụm từ bên câu hỏi và bài đọc , ta có: wind and sun = wind and solar most of Eigg’s electricity come from = Ei gg + most of its electricty from
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Background When Eigg designed its electricity grid, which was switched on in February 2008, it quickly became apparent that in order to keep the capital building costs down, it would be necessary to manage demand. This would also allow the island to generate most of its electricity from renewable sources, mainly water, wind and solar power."
explanation.step3: Dựa vào wind and sun -> tìm ra wind and solar power ở phần Background Đọc theo Linearthinking (Read in structure) để nắm ý chính, ta có: Question: Apart from wind and sun , where does most of Eigg’s electricity come from? Text : most of its electricity from renewable sources , mainly water, wind and solar power. => Đối chiếu 2 câu sẽ dễ dàng thấy được ngoài wind and sun -> còn thiếu water => Đáp án là water
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: water

questions.prompt: What device measures the amount of electricity Eigg’s households are using?

explanation.step1: Question : What device measures the amount of electricity Eigg’s households are using ? So sánh cụm từ bên câu hỏi và bài đọc , ta có: measures the amount of electricity Eigg’s households are using = display current and cumulative electricity usage device = energy monitors
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "The technology All households and businesses have energy monitors , which display current and cumulative electricity usage , and sound an alarm when consumption reaches a user-defined level, usually set a few hundred watts below the actual limit."
explanation.step3: Hiểu câu hỏi: What device measures the amount of electricity Eigg’s households are using? => Đáp án là danh từ - một thiết bị đo lượng điện tiêu thụ ở các Eigg's households => Cần đọc về 'device' -> Có thể thông tin sẽ xuất hiện ở đoạn 'Technology' => Từ đó thấy tìm thấy thông tin 'energy monitors' + 'display electricity usage' Câu tương đối dài, ta áp dụng đọc simplify với Linearthinking để nắm main idea All households and businesses have energy monitors , which display ... electricity usage , and sound an alarm when consumption reaches a user-defined level => Energy monitors - cho thấy electricity usage + báo động khi consumption đạt tới 1 level nhất định => Vậy ' energy monitors' chính là thiết bị đo lượng điện tiêu thụ => Answer: energy
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: energy monitors

questions.prompt: When renewable energy supplies are insufficient, what backs them up?

explanation.step1: Question : When renewable energy supplies are insufficient , what backs them up ? So sánh cụm từ bên câu hỏi và bài đọc , ta có: When renewable energy supplies are insufficient = when renewable energy generation is lower than demand backs them up = back it up
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Demand is also managed by warning the entire island when renewable energy generation is lower than demand , and diesel generators are operating to back it up - a so-called ‘red light day’, as opposed to ‘green light days’ when there is sufficient renewable energy."
explanation.step3: Hiểu câu hỏi: When renewable energy supplies are insufficient, what backs them up? => What backs them up? -> Đáp án là danh từ - một thứ đóng vai trò hỗ trợ khi thiếu renewable energy => Từ thông tin 'insufficient' , ta tìm được thông tin 'generation is lower than demand' >>> Ở đây ta cần phải biết từ 'insufficient ', nếu không sẽ rất khó làm nha, bạn nào chưa biết thì take note lại luôn vì đây là một từ khá phổ biến Áp dụng Linearthinking để nắm main idea: when renewable energy generation is lower than demand , and diesel generators are operating to back it up => Generation (sự phát điện/năng lượng) - thấp hơn - demand -> Cung thấp hơn cầu -> Insufficient => Dựa vào cụm 'back it up', dễ dàng nhận ra 'diesel generators' là danh từ cần tìm =
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: diesel generators

questions.prompt: What has EHT provided free of charge in all the houses it owns?

explanation.step1: Question : What has EHT provided free of charge in all the houses it owns ? So sánh cụm từ bên câu hỏi và bài đọc , ta có: EHT provided = Eigg Heritage Trust has installed free of charge in all the houses it owns = in all of its own properties at no cost
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "The technology Eigg Heritage Trust has installed insulation in all of its own properties at no cost to the tenants, while private properties have paid for their own insulation to be installed."
explanation.step3: Hiểu câu hỏi: What has EHT provided free of charge in all the houses it owns? => Đáp án là danh từ - thứ mà EHT cung cấp miễn phí => Dựa vào thông tin EHT + 'free of charge' , ta dễ dàng tìm thấy thông tin Áp dụng Linearthinking để nắm main idea: Eigg Heritage Trust has installed insulation in all of its own properties at no cost to the tenants => at no cost = free of charge = miễn phí => Thứ được EHT cung cấp miễn phí là 'insulation' => Answer: insulation
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: insulation

questions.prompt: Which gardening aid did some Eigg inhabitants claim grants for?

explanation.step1: Question : Which gardening aid did some Eigg inhabitants claim grants for? So sánh cụm từ bên câu hỏi và bài đọc , ta có: gardening aid = greenhouses to grow food locally inhabitants claim grants = Grants + residents can claim
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "The technology The Trust also operates a Green Grants scheme, where residents can claim 50 percent of the cost of equipment to reduce carbon emissions, up to a limit of £300. Purchases included bikes, solar water heating, secondary glazing, thicker curtains, and greenhouses to grow food locally , rather than importing it."
explanation.step3: Dựa vào keywords claim grants -> tìm thấy Grants và claim ở phần The technology Đọc theo Linearthinking (Read in structure) để nắm ý chính, ta có: 1 The Trust also operates a Green Grants scheme , where residents can claim 50 percent of the cost of equipment... 2 Purchases included ... and greenhouses to grow food locally, rather than importing it. Mà gardening aid = greenhouses to grow food locally => Đáp án là greenhouses Bạn nào không biết nghĩa locally vẫn có thể hiểu grow food = trồng thực phẩm -> tương đương gardening ; không hiểu nghĩa aid vẫn có thể suy ra đáp án là 1 trong số những cái gì đó vì câu hỏi dùng which (cái nào) Kết hợp 2 phân tích trên -> cần tìm 1 thứ gì đó (noun) ở gần grow food => Tìm thấy greenhouses ngay trước grow
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: greenhouses

questions.prompt: Electricity was available for the first time on Eigg when a new grid was switched on.

explanation.step1: Question: Electricity was available for the first time on Eigg when a new grid was switched on. So sánh cụm từ bên câu hỏi và bài đọc , ta có: when a new grid was switched on = installation of the new electricity grid Electricity was available for the first time # Prior to + used diesel generators to supply electricity
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Environmental benefits Prior to the installation of the new electricity grid and renewable energy generation, most households on Eigg used diesel generators to supply electricity, resulting in significant carbon emissions."
explanation.step3: Áp dụng Linearthinking để nắm main idea: Question : Electricity was available for the first time on Eigg when a new grid was switched on . Text : Prior to the installation of the new electricity grid... , most households on Eigg used diesel generators to supply electricity . => Trước khi có electricity grid - households on Eigg đã có điện rồi => C âu trả lời là FALSE Possible mistake: Nếu chỉ dựa vào keywords electricity grid và was switched on để tìm vị trí thông tin, bạn sẽ tìm thấy ở phần Background : When Eigg designed its electricity grid , which was switched on in February 2008, it quickly became apparent that in order to keep the capital building costs down, it would be necessary to manage demand. -> Kết luận vội là NOT GIVEN vì khôn
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: FALSE

questions.prompt: Eigg’s carbon emissions are now much lower than before.

explanation.step1: Question : Eigg’s carbon emissions are now much lower than before. So sánh cụm từ bên câu hỏi và bài đọc , ta có: Eigg’s carbon emissions = Domestic carbon emissions are now much lower = have fallen
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Environmental benefits Domestic carbon emissions have fallen by 47 percent, from 8.4 to 4.45 tonnes per year."
explanation.step3: Dựa vào keyword carbon emissions (liên quan tới environment ) để tìm đoạn chứa thông tin -> tìm thấy thông tin ở phần Environmental benefits. Áp dụng Linearthinking để nắm main idea: Domestic carbon emissions have fallen by 47 percent , from 8.4 to 4.45 tonnes per year. => Giảm 47% -> Much lower than before => Chọn TRUE
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: TRUE

questions.prompt: Wood will soon be the main source of heating on Eigg.

explanation.step1: Question : Wood will soon be the main source of heating on Eigg. So sánh cụm từ bên câu hỏi và bài đọc , ta có: wood = wood will be the main source of heating => Bài đọc không có info
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Environmental benefits The emissions should fall even further over the next few years as the supply of wood for heating increases."
explanation.step3: Hiểu câu hỏi: Wood will soon be the main source of heating on Eigg. => Wood sẽ trở thành nhiên liệu chính để sưởi ấm Áp dụng Linearthinking để nắm main idea: The emissions should fall even further over the next few years as the supply of wood for heating increases. => C02 emissions sẽ còn giảm nữa - vì - supply of wood for heating tăng => Nhiều bạn đọc tới đây sẽ vội vàng chọn TRUE => Tuy nhiên, việc lượng wood for heating tăng không đủ để kết luận rằng nó sẽ trở thành nhiên liệu chính cho việc heating => Chọn NOT GIVEN
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: NOT GIVEN

questions.prompt: Eigg is quieter as a result of having a new electricity supply.

explanation.step1: Question : Eigg is quieter as a result of having a new electricity supply . So sánh cụm từ bên câu hỏi và bài đọc , ta có: as a result of having a new electricity supply = A reliable electricity supply has brought quieter = elimination of the constant noise
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Social benefits A reliable electricity supply has brought improvements in other areas, for example, better treatment of drinking water in some houses, and the elimination of the constant noise of diesel generators."
explanation.step3: Dựa vào thông tin 'quieter', ta tìm các thông tin liên quan tới âm thanh/ tiếng ồn => Từ đó tìm được từ ' noise' + 'electricity supply' => Biết đó chính xác là thông tin cần đọc Đọc theo Linearthinking (Read in structure) để nắm ý chính, ta có: A reliable electricity supply has brought improvements , for example , better treatment ... and the elimination of the constant noise of diesel generators. => Từ khi có electricity supply - tiếng ồn của máy phát điện được loại bỏ >>> Nếu không hiểu 'elimination' , ta vẫn biết N1, N2 đang là các ví dụ về 'improvements' , nên chúng phải mang nghĩa tích cực >>> Từ đó có thể phần nào đoán được nghĩa của từ 'elimination' => Kết luận câu này TRUE
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: TRUE

questions.prompt: Well-off households pay higher prices for the use of extra electricity.

explanation.step1: Question : Well-off households pay higher prices for the use of extra electricity . So sánh cụm từ bên câu hỏi và bài đọc , ta có: use of extra electricity # If usage goes over the limit pay higher prices # electricity supply is cut off
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "The technology Eigg manages electricity demand mainly by capping the instantaneous power that can be used to five kilowatts (kW) for a household and ten kW for a business. If usage goes over the limit , the electricity supply is cut off and the maintenance team must be called to come and switch it back on again."
explanation.step3: Dựa vào thông tin ' use of extra electricity' -> tì m thấy thông tin ở phần The technology Vì thông tin nằm ở 2 câu, ta đọc connection với Linearthinking để nắm ý chính: 1 Eigg manages electricity demand mainly by capping the instantaneous power that can be used to five kilowatts (kW) for a household and ten kW for a business. 2 If usage goes over the limit , the electricity supply is cut off => Câu 1 cho biết Eigg giới hạn lượng điện sử dụng - 5kW cho household, 10kW cho doanh nghiệp => Câu 2 cho biết nếu dùng quá giới hạn - sẽ bị cắt điện => 1 + 2 : Household và business sẽ có lượng điện giới hạn nhất định - nếu vượt qua sẽ bị cắt điện => Gia đình nào cũng như nhau, không phân biệt well-off households hay gì cả => Chọn FALSE
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: FALSE

questions.prompt: The new electricity grid has created additional employment opportunities on Eigg.

explanation.step1: Question : The new electricity grid has created additional employment opportunities on Eigg. So sánh cụm từ bên câu hỏi và bài đọc , ta có: electricity grid = electricity grid has created additional employment opportunities = residents have also been employed
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Economic and employment benefits Eigg’s electricity grid supports four part-time maintenance jobs on the island, and residents have also been employed for building work to improve Trust-owned houses and other buildings."
explanation.step3: Dưa vào thông tin 'employment' của câu hỏi, ta biết cần đọc ở đoạn cuối - Economic and employment benefits Đọc theo Linearthinking (Read in structure) để nắm ý chính, ta có: Question : The new electricity grid has created additional employment opportunities on Eigg. Bài đọc : Eigg’s electricity grid supports four part-time maintenance jobs and residents have also been employed for building work => Eigg's electricity grid - đã hỗ trợ - 4 maintenance jobs - và - người dân cũng được thuê làm xây dựng => Eigg's electricity grid đã tạo ra nhiều cơ hội việc làm => Câu trả lời là TRUE
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: TRUE

passages.title: Change in business organisations
content: [A]  The forces that operate to bring about change in organisations can be thought of as winds which are many and varied - from small summer breezes that merely disturb a few papers, to mighty howling gales which cause devastation to structures and operations, causing consequent reorientation of purpose and rebuilding. Sometimes, however, the winds die down to give periods of relative calm, periods of relative organisational stability. Such a period was the agricultural age, which - Goodman (1995) - maintains prevailed in Europe and western societies as a whole until the early 1700s. During this period, wealth was created in the context of an agriculturally based society influenced mainly by local markets (both customer and labour) and factors outside people’s control, such as the weather. During this time, people could fairly well predict the cycle of activities required to maintain life, even if that life might be at little more than subsistence level.

[B]  To maintain the meteorological metaphor, stronger winds of change blew to bring in the Industrial Revolution and the industrial age. Again, according to Goodman, this lasted for a long time, until around 1945. It was characterised by a series of inventions and innovations that reduced the number of people needed to work the land and, in turn, provided the means of production of hitherto rarely obtainable goods; for organisations, supplying these in ever increasing numbers became the aim. To a large extent, demand and supply were predictable, enabling companies to structure their organisations along what Burns and Stalker (1966) described as mechanistic lines, that is as systems of strict hierarchical structures and firm means of control.

[C]  This situation prevailed for some time, with demand still coming mainly from the domestic market and organisations striving to fill the ‘supply gap’. Thus the most disturbing environmental influence on organisations of this time was the demand for products, which outstripped supply. The saying attributed to Henry Ford that ‘You can have any colour of car so long as it is black’, gives a flavour of the supply-led state of the market. Apart from any technical difficulties of producing different colours of car, Ford did not have to worry about customers’ colour preferences: he could sell all that he made. Organisations of this period can be regarded as ‘task oriented’, with effort being put into increasing production through more effective and efficient production processes.

[D]  As time passed, this favourable period for organisations began to decline. In the neo-industrial age, people became more discriminating in the goods and services they wished to buy and, as technological advancements brought about increased productivity, supply overtook demand. Companies began, increasingly, to look abroad for additional markets.

[E]  At the same time, organisations faced more intensive competition from abroad for their own products and services. In the West, this development was accompanied by a shift in focus from manufacturing to service, whether this merely added value to manufactured products, or whether it was service in its own right. In the neo industrial age of western countries, the emphasis moved towards adding value to goods and services - what Goodman calls the value-oriented time, as contrasted with the task- oriented and products/services-oriented times of the past.

[F]  Today, in the post-industrial age, most people agree that organisational life is becoming ever more uncertain, as the pace of change quickens and the future becomes less predictable. Writing in 1999, Nadler and Tushman, two US academics, said: ‘Poised on the eve of the next century, we are witnessing a profound transformation in the very nature of our business organisations. Historic forces have converged to fundamentally reshape the scope, strategies, and structures of large enterprises’. At a less general level of analysis, Graeme Leach, Chief Economist at the British Institute of Directors, claimed in the Guardian newspaper (2000) that: ‘By 2020, the nine-to-five rat race will be extinct and present levels of self-employment, commuting and technology use, as well as age and sex gaps, will have changed beyond recognition’. According to the article, Leach anticipates that: ‘In 20 years' time, 20-25 percent of the workforce will be temporary workers and many more will be flexible, ... 25 percent of people will no longer work in a traditional office and ... 50 percent will work from home in some form’. Continuing to use the ‘winds of change’ metaphor, the expectations of damaging gale-force winds bringing the need for rebuilding that takes the opportunity to incorporate new ideas and ways of doing things.

[G]  Whether all this will happen is arguable. Forecasting the future is always fraught with difficulties. For instance, Mannermann (1998) sees future studies as part art and part science and notes: ‘The future is full of surprises, uncertainty, trends and trend breaks, irrationality and rationality, and it is changing and escaping from our hands as time goes by. It is also the result of actions made by innumerable more or less powerful forces.’ What seems certain is that the organisational world is changing at a fast rate - even if the direction of change is not always predictable. Consequently, it is crucial that organisational managers and decision makers are aware of, and able to analyse the factors which trigger organisational change.

passages.title: The creation of lasting memories
content: 1. Many studies of the brain processes underlying the creation of memory consolidation (lasting memories) have involved giving various human and animal subjects treatment, while training them to perform a task. These have contributed greatly to our understanding.

2. In pioneering studies using goldfish, Bernard Agranoff found that protein synthesis inhibitors injected after training caused the goldfish to forget what they had learned. In other experiments, he administered protein synthesis inhibitors immediately before the fish were trained. The remarkable finding was that the fish learned the task completely normally, but forgot it within a few hours - that is, the protein synthesis inhibitors blocked memory consolidation, but did not influence short-term memory.

3. There is now extensive evidence that short-term memory is spared by many kinds of treatments, including electro-convulsive therapy (ECT), that block memory consolidation. On the other hand, and equally importantly, neuroscientist Ivan Izquierdo found that many drug treatments can block short-term memory without blocking memory consolidation. Contrary to the hypothesis put forward by Canadian psychologist Donald Hebb, in 1949, long-term memory does not require short-term memory, and vice versa.

Such findings suggest that our experiences create parallel, and possibly independent stages of memory, each with a different life span. All of this evidence from clinical and experimental studies strongly indicates that the brain handles recent and remote memory in different ways; but why does it do that?

5. We obviously need to have memory that is created rapidly: reacting to an ever and rapidly changing environment requires that. For example, most current building codes require that the heights of all steps in a staircase be equal. After taking a couple of steps, up or down, we implicitly remember the heights of the steps and assume that the others will be the same. If they are not the same, we are very likely to trip and fall. Lack of this kind of rapidly created implicit memory would be bad for us and for insurance companies, but perhaps good for lawyers. It would be of little value to us if we remembered the heights of the steps only after a delay of many hours, when the memory becomes consolidated.

6. The hypothesis that lasting memory consolidates slowly over time is supported primarily by clinical and experimental evidence that the formation of long-term memory is influenced by treatments and disorders affecting brain functioning. There are also other kinds of evidence indicating more directly that the memories consolidate over time after learning. Avi Kami and Dov Sagi reported that the performance of human subjects trained in a visual skill did not improve until eight hours after the training was completed, and that improvement was even greater the following day. Furthermore, the skill was retained for several years.

7. Studies using human brain imaging to study changes in neural activity induced by learning have also reported that the changes continue to develop for hours after learning. In an innovative study using functional imaging of the brain, Reza Shadmehr and Henry Holcomb examined brain activity in several brain regions shortly after human subjects were trained in a motor learning task requiring arm and hand movements. They found that while the performance of the subjects remained stable for several hours after completion of the training, their brain activity did not; different regions of the brain were predominantly active at different times over a period of several hours after the training. The activity shifted from the prefrontal cortex to two areas known to be involved in controlling movements, the motor cortex and cerebellar cortex. Consolidation of the motor skill appeared to involve activation of different neural systems that increased the stability of the brain processes underlying the skill.

8. There is also evidence that learning-induced changes in the activity of neurons in the cerebral cortex continue to increase for many days after the training. In an extensive series of studies using rats with electrodes implanted in the auditory cortex, Norman Weinberger reported that, after a tone of specific frequency was paired a few times with footshock, neurons in the rats’ auditory cortex responded more to that specific tone and less to other tones of other frequencies. Even more interestingly, the selectivity of the neurons’ response to the specific tone used in training continued to increase for several days after the training was terminated.

9. It is not intuitively obvious why our lasting memories consolidate slowly. Certainly, one can wonder why we have a form of memory that we have to rely on for many hours, days or a lifetime, that is so susceptible to disruption shortly after it is initiated. Perhaps the brain system that consolidates long-term memory over time was a late development in vertebrate evolution. Moreover, maybe we consolidate memories slowly because our mammalian brains are large and enormously complex. We can readily reject these ideas. All species of animals studied to date have both short and long-term memory; and all are susceptible to retrograde amnesia. Like humans, birds, bees, and molluscs, as well as fish and rats, make long-term memory slowly. Consolidation of memory clearly emerged early in evolution, and was conserved.

10. Although there seems to be no compelling reason to conclude that a biological system such as a brain could not quickly make a lasting memory, the fact is that animal brains do not. Thus, memory consolidation must serve some very important adaptive function or functions. There is considerable evidence suggesting that the slow consolidation is adaptive because it enables neurobiological processes occurring shortly after learning to influence the strength of memory for experiences. The extensive evidence that memory can be enhanced, as well as impaired, by treatments administered shortly after training, provides intriguing support for this hypothesis.

comparing the performance of different goldfish on certain tasks.
questions.correct: injecting goldfish at different stages of the experiments.

explanation.step1: Question : Experiments by Bernard Agranoff described in Reading Passage 3 involved Answer: A - injecting goldfish at different stages of the experiments So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: Bernard Agranoff = Bernard Agranoff injecting = injected = administered different stages of the experiments = after training + before the fish were trained
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "In pioneering studies using goldfish, Bernard Agranoff found that protein synthesis inhibitors injected after training caused the goldfish to forget what they had learned. In other experiments, he administered protein synthesis inhibitors immediately before the fish were trained ."
explanation.step3: Dựa vào tên riêng 'Bernard Agranoff' + 'gold fish' , ta dễ dàng tìm thấy thử nghiệm ở đoạn 2 Vì thông tin nằm ở 2 câu, ta đọc connection với Linearthinking : 1 In pioneering studies using goldfish , Bernard Agranoff found that protein synthesis inhibitors injected after training caused the goldfish to forget what they had learned. 2 In other experiments , he administered protein synthesis inhibitors immediately before the fish were trained. => Ta thấy có các từ lạ như 'synthsis inhibitors' , nhưng nếu đọc đúng cấu trúc - ta sẽ biết đó là một chất gì đó được tiêm vào goldfish => Sau đó dù không hiểu ' administered' là gì, nhờ đọc connection với câu 1 , ta thấy nó cũng đi với chất 'inhibitors' -> BIết administered = injected => 1 + 2 : Chất '
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: injecting goldfish at different stages of the experiments.

questions.prompt: Most findings from recent studies suggest that
options: drug treatments do not normally affect short-term memories.
long-term memories build upon short-term memories.
short and long-term memories are formed by separate processes.
ECT treatment affects both short-and long-term memories.
questions.correct: short and long-term memories are formed by separate processes.

explanation.step1: Question : Most findings from recent studies suggest that Answer: C - short and long-term memories are formed by separate processes . So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: findings + studies suggest that = Such findings suggest that short and long-term memories = each with a different life span separate processes = independent stages of memory
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Such findings suggest that our experiences create parallel, and possibly independent stages of memory , each with a different life span ."
explanation.step3: Khi đọc tới đoạn 3 , ta sẽ thấy 'There is now extensive evidence...' => Biết thông tin về 'recent studies' sẽ xuất hiện trong đoạn => Từ đó dựa vào từ 'findings' , ta xác định được thông tin cần đọc Áp dụng Linearthinking để nắm main idea: Such findings suggest that our experiences create parallel, and possibly independent stages of memory , each (stage) with a different life span. => Những findings cho thấy - trải nghiệm của ta - tạo ra - independent stages of memory - mỗi stage có life span khác nhau => Có thể một số bạn sẽ không hiểu 'life span', nhưng từ 'independent + stages' thì quá quen thuộc rồi => Khi so với đáp án, sẽ thấy chúng tương ứng với 'separate + processes' => Answer: C - short and long-term memories are formed by separate
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: short and long-term memories are formed by separate processes.

questions.prompt: In the fifth paragraph, what does the writer want to show by the example of staircases?
options: Prompt memory formation underlies the performance of everyday tasks.
Routine tasks can be carried out unconsciously.
Physical accidents can impair the function of memory.
Complex information such as regulations cannot be retained by the memory.
questions.correct: Prompt memory formation underlies the performance of everyday tasks.

explanation.step1: Question : In the fifth paragraph, what does the writer want to show by the example of staircases ? Answer: A - Prompt memory formation underlies the performance of everyday tasks. So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: staircases = staircase Prompt memory formation = memory that is created rapidly performance of everyday tasks = taking a couple of steps
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "We obviously need to have memory that is created rapidly : reacting to an ever and rapidly changing environment requires that. For example, most current building codes require that the heights of all steps in a staircase be equal. After taking a couple of steps , up or down, we implicitly remember the heights of the steps and assume that the others will be the same."
explanation.step3: Áp dụng đọc connection với Linearthinking để nắm main idea: 1 We obviously need to have memory that is created rapidly 2 For example , most current building codes require that the heights of all steps in a staircase be equal. 3 After taking a couple of steps , we implicitly remember the heights of the steps => Câu 1 đặt ra vấn đề về việc phải có ' memory that is created rapidly' => Câu 2 + 3 đưa ra ví dụ về staircase bổ sung cho câu 1 >>> Với việc ' đi cầu thang' có thể được hiểu là 'everyday task' => Main idea: việc đi cầu thang là ví dụ của việc tạo ra trí nhớ nhanh chóng => Ứng với đáp án A - Prompt memory formation underlies the performance of everyday tasks
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: Prompt memory formation underlies the performance of everyday tasks.

questions.prompt: Observations about memory by Kami and Sagi
options: were based on tasks involving hearing.

explanation.step1: Question : Observations about memory by Kami and Sagi Answer: D - confirmed other experimental findings. So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: Kami and Sagi = Avi Kami and Dov Sagi confirmed other experimental findings = other kinds of evidence indicating more directly that the memories consolidate over time after learning
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "There are also other kinds of evidence indicating more directly that the memories consolidate over time after learning . Avi Kami and Dov Sagi reported that the performance of human subjects trained in a visual skill did not improve until eight hours after the training was completed, and that improvement was even greater the following day. Furthermore, the skill was retained for several years."
explanation.step3: Áp dụng đọc connection với Linearthinking để nắm main idea: 1 There are also other kinds of evidence indicating that the memories consolidate over time after learning. 2 Avi Kami and Dov Sagi reported that the performance of human subjects trained in a visual skill did not improve until eight hours after the training was completed => Câu 1 cho biết có những evidence khác chỉ ra rằng - ký ức hình thành dần dần sau quá trình học => Câu 2 đưa ra ví dụ về thí nghiệm của Avi Kami and Dov Sagi bổ sung cho câu 1 : 8 tiếng sau khi tập luyện mới bắt đầu improve => Vậy có thể nói, tác giả nói về thí nghiệm của Kami + Sagi để confirm các evidence (findings) khác => Answer: D - confirmed other experimental findings
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: confirmed other experimental findings.

questions.prompt: What did the experiment by Shadmehr and Holcomb show?
options: Different areas of the brain were activated by different tasks.
Activity in the brain gradually moved from one area to other areas.
Subjects continued to get better at a task after training had finished.
Treatment given to subjects improved their performance on a task.
questions.correct: Activity in the brain gradually moved from one area to other areas.

explanation.step1: Question : What did the experiment by Shadmehr and Holcomb show? Answer: B - Activity in the brain gradually moved from one area to other areas So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: Shadmehr and Holcomb = They Activity in the brain gradually moved from one area to other area = different regions of the brain were predominantly active at different times
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "They found that while the performance of the subjects remained stable for several hours after completion of the training, their brain activity did not; different regions of the brain were predominantly active at different times over a period of several hours after the training."
explanation.step3: Dựa vào tên riêng 'Shadmehr and Holcomb' ta dễ dàng tìm được thông tin Áp dụng Linearthinking để nắm main idea: while the performance of the subjects remained stable , their brain activity did not ; different regions of the brain were predominantly active at different times => Trong khi - trạng thái của subjects đã ổn đinh - não họ vẫn hoạt động ; từng vùng khác nhau - hoạt động rõ rệt - vào từng thời điểm khác nhau => Lúc thì não hoạt active ở chỗ này - lúc thì ở chỗ khác -> Ứng với đáp án B - Activity in the brain gradually moved from one area to other area Nhiều bạn khi thấy câu A có nhắc tới 'different areas of the brain' có thể cũng sẽ thấy phân vân >>> Tuy nhiên, bài đọc không nói 'tasks' khiến nó active -> Loại A
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: Activity in the brain gradually moved from one area to other areas.

questions.prompt: The training which Kami and Sagi’s subjects were given was repeated over several days.

explanation.step1: Question : The training which Kami and Sagi ’s subjects were given was repeated over several days. So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: The training = the training Kami and Sagi = Avi Kami and Dov Sagi subjects = human subjects was repeated over several days => Bài đọc không có info
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Avi Kami and Dov Sagi reported that the performance of human subjects trained in a visual skill did not improve until eight hours after the training was completed, and that improvement was even greater the following day"
explanation.step3: Áp dụng Linearthinking để nắm main idea: Avi Kami and Dov Sagi reported that the performance of human subjects did not improve until eight hours after the training was completed , and that improvement was even greater the following day => 'The following day' là ngày tiếp theo - ta biết được trained thêm 1 ngày nữa => Tuy nhiên điều này chưa đủ để kết luận training được lặp lại trong nhiều ngày - cũng không thể kết luận là sai (chưa chắc là họ chỉ tập thêm 1 ngày hôm sau) => Chọn NOT GIVEN
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: NOT GIVEN

questions.prompt: The rats in Weinberger’s studies learned to associate a certain sound with a specific experience.

explanation.step1: Question : The rats in Weinberger ’s studies learned to associate a certain sound with a specific experience . So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: The rats = the rats Weinberger = Norman Weinberger learned to associate a certain sound = responded more to that specific tone specific experience = a tone of specific frequency was paired a few times with footshock
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Norman Weinberger reported that, after a tone of specific frequency was paired a few times with footshock , neurons in the rats ’ auditory cortex responded more to that specific tone and less to other tones of other frequencies."
explanation.step3: Áp dụng Linearthinking để nắm main idea: Norman Weinberger reported that , after a tone of specific frequency was paired a few times with footshock , neurons in the rats’ auditory cortex responded more to that specific tone >>> Thông tin nền: Ở thử nghiệm này, họ cấy electrode (bộ sốc điện) vào auditory cortex (bộ phận của não) ở chuột => S au nhiều lần shock (điện) - đi kèm với một tone (=sound) - thì - neurons của auditory cortex sẽ phản ứng mạnh mẽ hơn với các tones đó => Vậy experience ở đây là việc các chú chuột bị bị shock điện khi nghe một âm thanh cụ thể => Và qua experience này, chúng phản ứng đặc biệt mạnh mẽ hơn với các âm thanh đó -> Chúng đã learned các âm thanh - associate âm thanh đó với việc bị sốc điện => Ứng với câu hỏi ->
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: YES

questions.prompt: The results of Weinberger’s studies indicated that the strength of the rats’ learned associations increases with time

explanation.step1: Question : The results of Weinberger’s studies indicated that the strength of the rats’ learned associations increases with time So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: The results of Weinberger’s studies indicated that = Norman Weinberger reported that strength of the rats’ learned associations = the selectivity of the neurons’ response to the specific tone increases with time = increase for several days after the training was terminated
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Norman Weinberger reported that , after a tone of specific frequency was paired a few times with footshock, neurons in the rats’ auditory cortex responded more to that specific tone and less to other tones of other frequencies. Even more interestingly, the selectivity of the neurons’ response to the specific tone used in training continued to increase for several days after the training was terminated."
explanation.step3: Với tên riêng Norman Weinberger , ta nhanh chóng tìm ra thông tin cần đọc Vì thông tin phân mảnh ở 2 câu, ta đọc connection Linearthinking để nắm main idea: 1 Norman Weinberger reported that , after a tone of specific frequency was paired a few times with footshock , neurons in the rats’ auditory cortex responded more to that specific tone 2 Even more interestingly , the selectivity of the neurons’ response to the specific tone used in training continued to increase for several days after the training was terminated. >>> Thông tin nền: Ở thử nghiệm này, họ cấy electrode (bộ sốc điện) vào auditory cortex (bộ phận của não) ở chuột => Câu 1 cho biết sau nhiều lần shock (điện) - đi kèm với một tone nào đó - thì - neurons của auditory cortex sẽ
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: YES

questions.prompt: It is easy to see the evolutionary advantage of the way lasting memories in humans are created.

explanation.step1: Question : It is easy to see the evolutionary advantage of the way lasting memories in humans are created. So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: easy to see # not intuitively obvious lasting memories = lasting memories
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "It is not intuitively obvious why our lasting memories consolidate slowly."
explanation.step3: Vì dạng T/F/NG thường đi theo thứ tự từ trên xuống , sau khi làm câu trước ở đoạn 8, ta đọc tiếp và sẽ tìm thấy thông tin cho câu này Hiểu câu hỏi: : It is easy to see the evolutionary advantage of the way lasting memories in humans are created. => Dễ nhận ra lợi ích của cách mà lasting memorries được tạo ra Áp dụng Linearthinking để nắm main idea: It is not intuitively obvious why our lasting memories consolidate slowly. => Nếu bạn không hiểu 'intuitively' cũng không sao, ta vẫn hiểu là 'it is not obvious' => Obvious là hiển nhiên - dễ nhận thấy -> Not obvious = not easy to see => Không dễ nhận ra vì sao lasting memories lại hình thành chậm như vậy => Mâu thuẫn với câu hỏi -> Chọn FALSE
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: NO

questions.prompt: Long-term memories in humans are more stable than in many other species.

explanation.step1: Question : Long-term memories in humans are more stable than in many other species So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: Long-term memories = long-term memory are more stable => Bài đọc không có info many other species = birds, bees, and molluscs, as well as fish and rats
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "All species of animals studied to date have both short and long-term memory ; and all are susceptible to retrograde amnesia. Like humans, birds, bees, and molluscs, as well as fish and rats , make long-term memory slowly."
explanation.step3: Ở câu này nếu không đọc kĩ mà chỉ skim&scan , có khả năng sẽ chọn FALSE khi thấy 'all (species) are susceptible to retrograde amnesia' => Nghĩ tất cả các loài (bao gồm human) đều dễ mắc phải bệnh 'retrograde amnesia' -> không loài nào stable hơn loài nào -> FALSE => Sai >>> Tất cả đều mắc bệnh 'retrograde amnesia' (mất trí nhớ) - tuy nhiên, căn bệnh chỉ là một khía cạnh nhỏ, còn việc memories stable hay không là một khái niệm rộng hơn Ví dụ: một người bình thường và một người điên có thể về sau cũng sẽ trải qua việc mất trí nhớ - tuy nhiên - điều đó không có nghĩa là trí nhớ của người điên cũng stable như người thường >>> Không đủ thông tin để kết luận -> Chọn NOT GIVEN
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: NOT GIVEN

questions.prompt: Various researchers have examined the way lasting memories are formed. Laboratory experiments usually involve teaching subjects to do something _____ and treating them with mild electric shocks or drugs. Other studies monitor behaviour after a learning experience, or use sophisticated equipment to observe brain activity.

explanation.step1: Question : Laboratory experiments usually involve teaching subjects to do something new and treating them with mild electric shocks or drugs. So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: Laboratory experiments = studies teaching subjects to do something new = training them to perform a task treating them with mild electric shocks or drugs = giving various human and animal subjects treatment
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Many studies of the brain processes underlying the creation of memory consolidation (lasting memories) have involved giving various human and animal subjects treatment , while training them to perform a task. These have contributed greatly to our understanding."
explanation.step3: Title của summary là long-term memory khá là chung chung (vì cả bài này đều nói về long-term memory) => Có thể đây là summary của cả bài -> Bắt đầu tìm thông tin từ đoạn đầu Áp dụng Linearthinking để nắm main idea: Many studies of the brain processes underlying... have involved giving various human and animal subjects treatment , while training them to perform a task. => Nhiều nghiên cứu về não - đã thực hiện treatment với các đối tượng - trong khi - luyện cho họ thực hiện một task => Luyện cho thực hiện một task -> Dạy một task mới cho họ => So với danh sách đáp án -> Phù hợp nhất là F - new
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: F. new

questions.prompt: The results are generally consistent: they show that lasting memories are the result of a _____ and complex biological process.

explanation.step1: Question : The results are generally consistent: they show that lasting memories are the result of a lengthy and complex biological process So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: lasting memories = lasting memory len gth y = slowly
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "The hypothesis that lasting memory consolidates slowly over time"
explanation.step3: Hiểu câu hỏi: The results are generally consistent: they show that lasting memories are the result of a _____ and complex biological process => 'The results', tìm đọc về kết quả của các nghiên cứu trong bài (các đoạn 6,7,8) => Và thường một đoạn sẽ bắt đầu với Topic sentence , chỉ ra kết quả nghiên cứu - rồi mới giải thích bằng thử nghiệm -> Chỉ cần đọc câu đầu là đủ Áp dụng Linearthinking để nắm main idea: The hypothesis that lasting memory consolidates slowly over time => Lasting memory - trở nên bền vững - slowly => So với đáp án -> Phù hợp nhất là E - lengthy >>> Và memory consolidation cũng còn nhiều tính chất khác , rút ra từ nhiều cuộc thử nghiệm -> Có lẽ vì vậy mà họ dùng từ 'complex' , chứ nếu bạn skim&scan theo từ 'complex' thì sẽ
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: E. lengthy

questions.prompt: The fact that humans share this trait with other species, including animals with _____ brains, suggests that it developed _____ in our evolutionary history.

explanation.step1: Question : The fact that humans share this trait with other species , including animals with small brain So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: humans share this trait with other species = All species of animals studied to date have both short and long-term memory brain = brains
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Moreover, maybe we consolidate memories slowly because our mammalian brains are large and enormously complex. We can readily reject these ideas. All species of animals studied to date have both short and long-term memory"
explanation.step3: Khi thấy thông tin về việc so sánh người với động vật - ta nghĩ ngay tới đoạn liệt kê rất nhiều loại động vật Áp dụng Linearthinking để nắm main idea: 1 Moreover , maybe we consolidate memories slowly because our mammalian brains are large and enormously complex. 2 We can readily reject these ideas. 3 All species of animals have both short and long-term memory => Câu 1 đưa ra giả định : có lẽ ta consolidate memories slowly vì - não của ta lớn và phức tạp hơn => Câu 2 nói ta có thể bác bỏ quan niệm ở câu 1 => Câu 3 cho biết tất cả các loài - đều có short and long-term memory (tất cả các loài đều như nhau) => Main idea: Dù não to hay nhỏ thì cũng giống nhau So với câu hỏi: The fact that humans share this trait with other species, including an
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: H. small

explanation.step1: Question : it developed early in our evolutionary history. So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: it developed early in our evolutionary history = Consolidation of memory clearly emerged early in evolution
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Consolidation of memory clearly emerged early in evolution , and was conserved."
explanation.step3: Hiểu câu hỏi: it developed ____ in our evolutionary history. => Đáp án là trạng từ (bổ nghĩa cho động từ 'developed') => Chỉ có 2 options phù hợp: early + recently => Ở đây 'it' được dùng để chỉ ' lasting memories' = memory consolidation (đoạn 1 có đề cập) => Ta cần tìm xem memory consolidation tiến hóa từ sớm hay gần đây Áp dụng Linearthinking để nắm main idea: Consolidation of memory clearly emerged early in evolution => Answer: early

plus-3-reading-2.title: IELTS Practice Test Plus 3 - Reading Test 2

passages.title: Sport Science in Australia
content: The professional career paths available to graduates from courses relating to human movement and sport science are as diverse as the graduate’s imagination. However, undergraduate courses with this type of content, in Australia as well as in most other Western countries, were originally designed as preparation programmes for Physical Education (PE) teachers.

The initial programmes commenced soon after the conclusion of World War II in the mid-1940s. One of the primary motives for these initiatives was the fact that, during the war effort, so many of the men who were assessed for military duty had been declared unfit. The government saw the solution in the providing of Physical Education programmes in schools, delivered by better prepared and specifically educated PE teachers.

Later, in the 1970s and early 1980s, the surplus of Australians graduating with a PE degree obliged institutions delivering this qualification to identify new employment opportunities for their graduates, resulting in the first appearance of degrees catering for recreation professionals. In many instances, this diversity of programme delivery merely led to degrees, delivered by physical educators, as a side­line activity to the production of PE teachers.

Whilst the need to produce Physical Education teachers remains a significant social need, and most developed societies demand the availability of quality leisure programmes for their citizens, the career options of graduates within this domain are still developing. The two most evident growth domains are in the area of the professional delivery of sport, and the role of a physical lifestyle for community health.

The sports industry is developing at an unprecedented rate of growth. From a business perspective, sport is now seen as an area with the potential for high returns. It is quite significant that the businessman Rupert Murdoch broadened his business base from media to sport, having purchased an American baseball team and an Australian Rugby League competition, as well as seeking opportunities to invest in an English football club. No business person of such international stature would see fit to invest in sport unless he was satisfied that this was a sound business venture with ideal revenue-generating opportunities.

These developments have confirmed sport as a business with professional management structures, marketing processes, and development strategies in place. They have indicated new and developing career paths for graduates of human movement science, sport science, exercise science and related degrees. Graduates can now visualise career paths extending into such diverse domains as sport management, sport marketing, event and facility management, government policy development pertaining to sport, sport journalism, sport psychology, and sport or athletic coaching.

Business leaders will only continue their enthusiasm for sport if they receive returns for their money. Such returns will only be forthcoming if astute, enthusiastic and properly educated professionals are delivering the programs that earn appropriate financial returns. The successful universities of the 21st century will be those that have responded to this challenge by delivering such degrees.

A second professional growth area for this group of graduates is associated with community health. The increasing demand for government expenditure within health budgets is reaching the stage where most governments are simply unable to function in a manner that is satisfying their constituents. One of the primary reasons for this problem is the unhelpful emphasis on treatment in medical care programmes. Governments have traditionally given their senior health official the title of ‘Minister for Health’, when in fact this officer has functioned as ‘Minister for Sickness and the Construction of Hospitals’. Government focus simply has to change. If the change is not brought about for philosophical reasons, it will occur naturally, because insufficient funding will be available to address the ever-increasing costs of medical support.

Graduates of human movement, exercise science and sport science have the potential to become major players in this shift in policy focus. It is these graduates who already have the skills, knowledge and understanding to initiate community health education programmes to reduce cardio-vascular disease, to reduce medical dependency upon diabetes, to improve workplace health leading to increased productivity, to initiate and promote programmes of activity for the elderly that reduce medical dependency, and to maintain an active lifestyle for the unemployed and disadvantaged groups in society. This is the graduate that governments will be calling upon to shift the community focus from medical dependency to healthy lifestyles in the decades ahead.

The career paths of these graduates are developing at a pace that is not evident in other professions. The contribution that these graduates can make to society, and the recognition of this contribution is at an unprecedented high, and all indications are that it will continue to grow

passages.title: An assessment of micro-wind turbines
content: [A]  In terms of micro-renewable energy sources suitable for private use, a 15-kilowatt (kW) turbine is at the biggest end of the spectrum. With a nine metre diameter and a pole as high as a four-storey house, this is the most efficient form of wind micro­turbine, and the sort of thing you could install only if you had plenty of space and money. According to one estimate, a 15-kW micro-turbine (that’s one with the maximum output), costing £41,000 to purchase and a further £9,000 to install, is capable of delivering 25,000 kilowatt-hours (kWh)’ of electricity each year if placed on a suitably windy site.

[B]  I don’t know of any credible studies of the greenhouse gas emissions involved in producing and installing turbines, so my estimates here are going to be even more broad than usual. However, it is worth trying. If turbine manufacture is about as carbon intensive per pound sterling of product as other generators and electrical motors, which seems a reasonable assumption, the carbon intensity of manufacture will be around 640 kilograms (kg) per £1,000 of value. Installation is probably about as carbon intensive as typical construction, at around 380 kg per £1,000. That makes the carbon footprint (the total amount of greenhouse gases that installing a turbine creates) 30 tonnes.

[C]  The carbon savings from wind-powered electricity generation depend on the carbon intensity of the electricity that you’re replacing. Let’s assume that your generation replaces the coal-fueled part of the country’s energy mix. In other words, if you live in the UK, let’s say that rather than replacing typical grid electricity, which comes from a mix of coal, gas, oil and renewable energy sources, the effect of your turbine is to reduce the use of coal-fired power stations. That’s reasonable, because coal is the least preferable source in the electricity mix. In this case the carbon saving is roughly one kilogram per kWh, so you save 25 tonnes per year and pay back the embodied carbon in just 14 months - a great start.

[D]  The UK government has recently introduced a subsidy for renewable energy that pays individual producers 24p per energy unit on top of all the money they save on their own fuel bill, and on selling surplus electricity back to the grid at approximately 5p per unit. With all this taken into account, individuals would get back £7,250 per year on their investment. That pays back the costs in about six years. It makes good financial sense and, for people who care about the carbon savings for their own sake, it looks like a fantastic move. The carbon investment pays back in just over a year, and every year after that is a 25-tonne carbon saving. (It’s important to remember that all these sums rely on a wind turbine having a favourable location)

[E]  So, at face value, the turbine looks like a great idea environmentally, and a fairly good long-term investment economically for the person installing it. However, there is a crucial perspective missing from the analysis so far. Has the government spent its money wisely? It has invested 24p per unit into each micro-turbine. That works out at a massive £250 per tonne of carbon saved. My calculations tell me that had the government invested its money in offshore wind farms, instead of subsidising smaller domestic turbines, they would have broken even after eight years. In other words, the micro-turbine works out as a good investment for individuals, but only because the government spends, and arguably wastes, so much money subsidizing it. Carbon savings are far lower too.

[F]  Nevertheless, although the micro-wind turbine subsidy doesn’t look like the very best way of spending government resources on climate change mitigation, we are talking about investing only about 0.075 percent per year of the nation’s GDP to get a one percent reduction in carbon emissions, which is a worthwhile benefit. In other words, it could be much better, but it could be worse. In addition, such investment helps to promote and sustain developing technology.

[G]  There is one extra favourable way of looking at the micro-wind turbine, even if it is not the single best way of investing money in cutting carbon. Input- output modelling has told us that it is actually quite difficult to spend money without having a negative carbon impact. So if the subsidy encourages people to spend their money on a carbon-reducing technology such as a wind turbine, rather than on carbon-producing goods like cars, and services such as overseas holidays, then the reductions in emissions will be greater than my simple sums above have suggested.

passages.title: Pottery production in ancient Akrotiri
content: Excavations at the site of prehistoric Akrotiri, on the coast of the Aegean Sea, have revealed much about the technical aspects of pottery manufacture, indisputably one of the basic industries of this Greek city. However, considerably less is known about the socio-economic context and the way production was organised.

The bulk of pottery found at Akrotiri is locally made, and dates from the late fifteenth century BC. It clearly fulfilled a vast range of the settlement’s requirements: more than fifty different types of pots can be distinguished. The pottery found includes a wide variety of functional types like storage jars, smaller containers, pouring vessels, cooking pots, drinking vessels and so on, which all relate to specific activities and which would have been made and distributed with those activities in mind. Given the large number of shapes produced and the relatively high degree of standardization, it has generally been assumed that most, if not all, of Akrotiri pottery was produced by specialized craftsmen in a non­domestic context. Unfortunately neither the potters’ workshops nor kilns have been found within the excavated area. The reason may be that the ceramic workshops were located on the periphery of the site, which has not yet been excavated. In any event, the ubiquity of the pottery, and the consistent repetition of the same types in different sizes, suggests production on an industrial scale.

The Akrotirian potters seem to have responded to pressures beyond their households, namely to the increasing complexity of regional distribution and exchange systems. We can imagine them as full­time craftsmen working permanently in a high production-rate craft such as pottery manufacture, and supporting themselves entirely from the proceeds of their craft. In view of the above, one can begin to speak in terms of mass-produced pottery and the existence of organized workshops of craftsmen during the period 1550-1500 BC. Yet, how pottery production was organized at Akrotiri remains an open question, as there is no real documentary evidence. Our entire knowledge comes from the ceramic material itself, and the tentative conclusions which can be drawn from it.

The invention of units of quantity and of a numerical system to count them was of capital importance for an exchange-geared society such as that of Akrotiri. In spite of the absence of any written records, the archaeological evidence reveals that concepts of measurements, both of weight and number, had been formulated. Standard measures may already have been in operation, such as those evidenced by a graduated series of lead weights - made in disc form - found at the site. The existence of units of capacity in Late Bronze Age times is also evidenced by the notation of units of a liquid measure for wine on excavated containers.

It must be recognized that the function of pottery vessels plays a very important role in determining their characteristics. The intended function affects the choice of clay, the production technique, and the shape and the size of the pots. For example, large storage jars (pithoi) would be needed to store commodities, whereas smaller containers would be used for transport. In fact, the length of a man’s arm limits the size of a smaller pot to a capacity of about twenty litres; that is also the maximum a man can comfortably carry.

The various sizes of container would thus represent standard quantities of a commodity, which is a fundamental element in the function of exchange. Akrotirian merchants handling a commodity such as wine would have been able to determine easily the amount of wine they were transporting from the number of containers they carried in their ships, since the capacity of each container was known to be 14-18 litres. (We could draw a parallel here with the current practice in Greece of selling oil in 17 kilogram tins)

We may therefore assume that the shape, capacity, and, sometimes decoration of vessels are indicative of the commodity contained by them. Since individual transactions would normally involve different quantities of a given commodity, a range of ‘standardized’ types of vessel would be needed to meet traders’ requirements.

In trying to reconstruct systems of capacity by measuring the volume of excavated pottery, a rather generous range of tolerances must be allowed. It seems possible that the potters of that time had specific sizes of vessel in mind, and tried to reproduce them using a specific type and amount of clay. However, it would be quite difficult for them to achieve the exact size required every time, without any mechanical means of regulating symmetry and wall thickness, and some potters would be more skilled than others. In addition, variations in the repetition of types and size may also occur because of unforeseen circumstances during the throwing process. For instance, instead of destroying the entire pot if the clay in the rim contained a piece of grit, a potter might produce a smaller pot by simply cutting off the rim. Even where there is no noticeable external difference between pots meant to contain the same quantity of a commodity, differences in their capacity can actually reach one or two litres. In one case the deviation from the required size appears to be as much as 10-20 percent.

The establishment of regular trade routes within the Aegean led to increased movement of goods; consequently a regular exchange of local, luxury and surplus goods, including metals, would have become feasible as a result of the advances in transport technology. The increased demand for standardized exchanges, inextricably linked to commercial transactions, might have been one of the main factors which led to the standardization of pottery production. Thus, the whole network of ceramic production and exchange would have depended on specific regional economic conditions, and would reflect the socio-economic structure of prehistoric Akrotiri.
