explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: little-finger bone

passages.title: The Future of fish
content: The face of the ocean has changed completely since the first commercial fishers cast their nets and hooks over a thousand years ago. Fisheries intensified over the centuries, but even by the nineteenth century it was still felt, justifiably, that the plentiful resources of the sea were for the most part beyond the reach of fishing, and so there was little need to restrict fishing or create protected areas. The twentieth century heralded an escalation in fishing intensity that is unprecedented in the history of the oceans, and modern fishing technologies leave fish no place to hide. Today, the only refuges from fishing are those we deliberately create. Unhappily, the sea trails far behind the land in terms of the area and the quality of protection given.

For centuries, as fishing and commerce have expanded, we have held onto the notion that the sea is different from the land. We still view it as a place where people and nations should be free to come and go at will, as well as somewhere that should be free for us to exploit. Perhaps this is why we have been so reluctant to protect the sea. On land, protected areas have proliferated as human populations have grown. Here, compared to the sea, we have made greater headway in our struggle to maintain the richness and variety of wildlife and landscape. Twelve percent of the world’s land is now contained in protected areas, whereas the corresponding figure for the sea is but three-fifths of one percent. Worse still, most marine protected areas allow some fishing to continue. Areas off-limits to all exploitation cover something like one five-thousandth of the total area of the world’s seas.

Today, we are belatedly coming to realize that ‘natural refuges’ from fishing have played a critical role in sustaining fisheries, and maintaining healthy and diverse marine ecosystems. This does not mean that marine reserves can rebuild fisheries on their own - other management measures are also required for that. However, places that are off-limits to fishing constitute the last and most important part of our package of reform for fisheries management. They underpin and enhance all our other efforts. There are limits to protection though.

Reserves cannot bring back what has died out. We can never resurrect globally extinct species, and restoring locally extinct animals may require reintroductions from elsewhere, if natural dispersal from remaining populations is insufficient. We are also seeing, in cases such as northern cod in Canada, that fishing can shift marine ecosystems into different states, where different mixes of species prevail. In many cases, these species are less desirable, since the prime fishing targets have gone or are much reduced in numbers, and changes may be difficult to reverse, even with a complete moratorium on fishing. The Mediterranean sailed by Ulysses, the legendary king of ancient Greece, supported abundant monk seals, loggerhead turtles and porpoises. Their disappearance through hunting and overfishing has totally restructured food webs, and recovery is likely to be much harder to achieve than their destruction was. This means that the sooner we act to protect marine life, the more certain will be our success.

To some people, creating marine reserves is an admission of failure. According to their logic, reserves should not be necessary if we have done our work properly in managing the uses we make of the sea. Many fisheries managers are still wedded to the idea that one day their models will work, and politicians will listen to their advice. Just give the approach time, and success will be theirs. How much time have we got? This approach has been tried and refined for the last 50 years. There have been few successes which to feather the managers’ caps, but a growing litany of failure. The Common Fisheries Policy, the European Union’s instrument for the management of fisheries and aquaculture, exemplifies the worst pitfalls: flawed models, flawed advice, watered-down recommendations from government bureaucrats and then the disregard of much of this advice by politicians. When it all went wrong, as it inevitably had to, Europe sent its boats to other countries in order to obtain fish for far less than they were actually worth.

We are squandering the wealth of oceans. If we don’t break out of this cycle of failure, humanity will lose a key source of protein, and much more besides. Disrupting natural ecosystem processes, such as water purification, nutrient cycling, and carbon storage, could have ramifications for human life itself. We can go a long way to avoiding this catastrophic mistake with simple common sense management. Marine reserves lie at the heart of the reform. But they will not be sufficient if they are implemented only here and there to shore up the crumbling edifice of the ‘rational fisheries management’ envisioned by scientists in the 1940s and 1950s. They have to be placed centre stage as a fundamental underpinning for everything we do in the oceans. Reserves are a first resort, not a final resort when all else fails.
NOTE: Species reintroduction is the deliberate release of a species into the wild, from captivity or other areas where the animal survives.

questions.prompt: It is more than a thousand years since people started to catch fish for commercial use.

explanation.step1: Question : It is more than a thousand years since people started to catch fish for commercial use . So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: more than a thousand years = over a thousand years ago people started to catch fish for commercial use = the first commercial fishers cast their nets and hooks
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "The face of the ocean has changed completely since the first commercial fishers cast their nets and hooks over a thousand years ago ."
explanation.step3: Ở câu này câu hỏi chỉ đơn thuần là thay đổi cấu trúc câu , ta chỉ cần Read-ín-structure với LInearthinking sẽ thấy ngay Câu hỏi: It is more than a thousand years since people started to catch fish for commercial use. Bài đọc: the first commercial fishers cast their nets and hooks over a thousand years ago => Ta có cấu trúc: It is + time + since + S-V = S-V + time + ago => Lấy một ví dụ đơn giản nha: It is 5 days since I met Tom = I met Tom five days ago => Các thông tin trong bài đọc và câu hỏi đều ứng với nhau -> Chọn YES
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: YES

questions.prompt: In general, open access to the oceans is still regarded as desirable.

explanation.step1: Question : In general, open access to the oceans is still regarded as desirable. So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: open access = free to come and go at will + free for us to exploit is still regarded = we still view it
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "For centuries, as fishing and commerce have expanded, we have held onto the notion that the sea is different from the land. We still view it as a place where people and nations should be free to come and go at will , as well as somewhere that should be free for us to exploit ."
explanation.step3: Áp dụng Linearthinking để nắm main idea: Hiểu câu hỏi: In general , open access to the oceans is still regarded as desirable. => ' Desirable' có nghĩa là ' đáng khát khao' -> X is regarded as desirable = X is wanted => Mọi người wanted to have open access to oceans Phân tích info: We still view it as a place where people and nations should be free to come and go at will , as well as somewhere that should be free for us to exploit. => Ta vẫn xem oceans là nơi - moi người có thể free to come and go at will + free to exploit => Tự do đến và khai thác = have open access => Chọn YES
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: YES

questions.prompt: Sea fishing is now completely banned in the majority of protected areas.

explanation.step1: Question : Sea fishing is now completely banned in the majority of protected areas . So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: Sea fishing is now completely banned # allow some fishing to continue the majority of protected areas = most marine protected areas
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Worse still, most marine protected areas allow some fishing to continue ."
explanation.step3: Áp dụng Linearthinking để nắm main idea: Worse still , most marine protected areas allow some fishing to continue. => Hầu hết các protected areas - cho phép việc đánh bắt cá diễn ra => Sea fishing is not completely banned -> Chọn NO
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: NO

questions.prompt: People should be encouraged to reduce the amount of fish they eat.

explanation.step1: Question : People should be encouraged to reduce the amount of fish they eat. So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: People should be encouraged to reduce the amount of fish they eat. => Bài đọc không có info
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "This does not mean that marine reserves can rebuild fisheries on their own - other management measures are also required for that."
explanation.step3: Ta thấy đoạn 3 bắt đầu nói về việc 'maintaining healthy and diverse marine ecosystems' + 'fisheries management' => Biết đang xoay quanh vấn đề bảo tồn -> Cần đọc xem có thông tin về việc giảm lượng cá tiêu thụ không Áp dụng Linearthinking để nắm main idea: This does not mean that marine reserves can rebuild fisheries on their own - other management measures are also required for that. => Một mình 'marine reserves' là không đủ - cần các management measures khác => Tuy nhiên không nói cụ thể các measures đó là gì => Không đề cập tới việc giảm lượng cá tiêu thụ -> Chọn NOT GIVEN
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: NOT GIVEN

questions.prompt: The re-introduction of certain mammals to the Mediterranean is a straightforward task.

explanation.step1: Question : The re-introduction of certain mammals to the Mediterranean is a straightforward task. So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: The re-introduction = recovery certain mammals = monk seals, loggerhead turtles and porpoises. is a straightforward task # is likely to be much harder to achieve
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "The Mediterranean sailed by Ulysses, the legendary king of ancient Greece, supported abundant monk seals, loggerhead turtles and porpoises. Their disappearance through hunting and overfishing has totally restructured food webs, and recovery is likely to be much harder to achieve than their destruction was"
explanation.step3: Dựa vào tên riêng 'Mediterranean' + tên một số loài động vật , ta nhanh chóng tìm được thông tin cần đọc Áp dụng Linearthinking để nắm main idea: Their disappearance through hunting and overfishing has totally restructured food webs , and recovery is likely to be much harder to achieve than their destruction was => Việc biến mất của các loài mammals trên - đã làm thay đổi mạng lưới thức ăn - và - việc recovery (reintroduction) - là rất khó thực hiện >>> Trong trường hợp không biết từ 'straightforward' , ta có thể đoán nghĩa nó nha >>> 'Straight' là thẳng, 'forward' là tiến tới -> Tiến thắng tới thì có thể hiểu là không gặp trở ngại gì -> So với 'harder to achieve', đoán được 'straight forward' có nghĩa là 'dễ' => Chọn NO
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: NO

questions.prompt: What does the writer mean with the question, ‘How much time have we got?’ in the fifth paragraph?
options: Fisheries policies are currently based on uncertain estimates.
Accurate predictions will allow governments to plan properly.
Fisheries managers should provide clearer information.
Action to protect fish stocks is urgently needed
questions.correct: Action to protect fish stocks is urgently needed

explanation.step1: Question : What does the writer mean with the question, ‘How much time have we got? ’ in the fifth paragraph Answer: D - Action to protect fish stocks is urgently needed So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: How much time have we got? = How much time have we got? Action to protect fish stocks = reserves
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "According to their logic, reserves should not be necessary if we have done our work properly in managing the uses we make of the sea. Many fisheries managers are still wedded to the idea that one day their models will work, and politicians will listen to their advice. Just give the approach time, and success will be theirs. How much time have we got? This approach has been tried and refined for the last 50 years."
explanation.step3: Ở câu này ta sẽ phải hiểu ngụ ý của câu hỏi để có thể rút ra đáp án Do đó, ta cần đọc connection giữa các câu với Linearthinking để rút ra main idea: 1 According to their logic , reserves should not be necessary if we have done our work properly in managing the uses we make of the sea. 2 Many fisheries managers are still wedded to the idea that one day their models will work , and politicians will listen to their advice. 3 Just give the approach time , and success will be theirs. 4 How much time have we got? 5 This approach has been tried and refined for the last 50 years. => Câu 1 : việc reserves sẽ không cần thiết nếu ta tận dụng the sea đúng cách => Câu 2 : nhiều fisheries managers vẫn tin rằng một ngày nào đó mô hình của họ sẽ thành côn
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: Action to protect fish stocks is urgently needed

options: Measures that it advocated were hastily implemented.
Officials exaggerated some of its recommendations.
It was based on predictions which were inaccurate.
The policy makers acquired a good reputation
questions.correct: It was based on predictions which were inaccurate.

explanation.step1: Question : What is the writer’s comment on the Common Fisheries Policy ? Answer: C - It was based on predictions which were inaccurate . So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: Common Fisheries Policy = Common Fisheries Policy inaccurate = flawed + went wrong
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "The Common Fisheries Policy , the European Union’s instrument for the management of fisheries and aquaculture, exemplifies the worst pitfalls: flawed models, flawed advice, watered-down recommendations from government bureaucrats and then the disregard of much of this advice by politicians. When it all went wrong , as it inevitably had to"
explanation.step3: Nếu chỉ skim&scan , ta có thể tìm thấy thông tin thông qua 'Common Fisheries Policy ', tuy nhiên, câu này nếu không đọc hiểu kĩ sẽ khó rút ra đáp án Áp dụng Linearthinking để nắm main idea: 1 The Common Fisheries Policy , exemplifies the worst pitfalls : flawed models , flawed advice , watered-down recommendations from government bureaucrats and then the disregard of much of this advice by politicians. 2 When it all went wrong , as it inevitably had to ... => Câu 1 cho biết lấy ví dụ về Common Fisheries Policy - flawed models, flawed advice,... => Câu 2 cho biết tất cả những điều liệt kê trên kiểu gì cũng sẽ go wrong >>> 'Model ' ở đây có thể hiểu là 'plan' -> Để có thể vạch ra 'model' + 'advice' , chắc chắn là họ phải dựa trên các dự đoán
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: It was based on predictions which were inaccurate.

questions.prompt: What is the writer’s conclusion concerning the decline of marine resources?
options: The means of avoiding the worst outcomes needs to be prioritized.
Measures already taken to avoid a crisis are probably sufficient.
The situation is now so severe that there is no likely solution.
It is no longer clear which measures would be most effective.
questions.correct: The means of avoiding the worst outcomes needs to be prioritized.

explanation.step1: Question : What is the writer’s conclusion concerning the decline of marine resources? Answer: A - The means of avoiding the worst outcomes needs to be prioritized . So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: The means of avoiding the worst outcomes = marine reserves + Reserves needs to be prioritized = have to be placed centre stage + are a first resort
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "We can go a long way to avoiding this catastrophic mistake with simple common sense management. Marine reserves lie at the heart of the reform. But they will not be sufficient if they are implemented only here and there to shore up the crumbling edifice of the ‘rational fisheries management’ envisioned by scientists in the 1940s and 1950s. They have to be placed centre stage as a fundamental underpinning for everything we do in the oceans. Reserv"
explanation.step3: Vì thông tin phân mảnh, ta đọc connection với Linearthinking để nắm main idea: 1 Marine reserves lie at the heart of the reform. 2 But they will not be sufficient if they are implemented only here and there 3 They have to be placed centre stage as a fundamental underpinnin g for everything we do in the oceans. 4 Reserves are a first resort , not a final resort when all else fails. => Câu 1 cho biết 'marine reserves' là điều quan trọng nhất của việc cải cách => Câu 2 nói rằng nhưng nếu chỉ áp dụng lưa thưa thì sẽ không hiệu quả ( here and there nghĩa là ở đây 1 miếng, ở kia 1 miếng ) => Câu 3 cho biết chúng phải được xem là quan trọng nhất - là nền tảng chính - đối với tất cả những gì chúng ta làm ở đại dương => Câu 4 chốt lại: reserves là f
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: The means of avoiding the worst outcomes needs to be prioritized.

questions.prompt: Up till the twentieth century the world’s supply of fish was sufficient for its needs.

explanation.step1: Question : It was unnecessary to introduce controls of any kind , because large areas of the oceans were inaccessible . So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: unnecessary to introduce controls of any kind = there was little need to restrict fishing or create protected areas large areas of the oceans were inaccessible = the plentiful resources of the sea were for the most part beyond the reach of fishing
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "the plentiful resources of the sea were for the most part beyond the reach of fishing , and so there was little need to restrict fishing or create protected areas."
explanation.step3: Áp dụng Linearthinking để nắm main idea: the plentiful resources of the sea were for the most part beyond the reach of fishing , and so there was little need to restrict fishing or create protected areas. => 'Beyond' có nghĩa là 'vượt trên một mức nào đó' -> 'Beyond the reach of fishing' có thể hiểu là 'không đánh bắt cá được' => Vẫn chưa đánh bắt/tiếp cận được ở phần lớn đại dương - nên - không cần phải (unecessary) restrict fishing hay create protected areas => Restrict fishing + create protected areas là những cách để kiểm soát việc đánh bắt cá => So với đáp án -> Chọn được đáp án B - controls
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: B. controls

questions.prompt: It was unnecessary to introduce _____ of any kind, because large areas of the oceans were inaccessible.

explanation.step1: Question : However, as fishing techniques improved , this situation changed , and in the middle of the twentieth century So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: fishing techniques improved = modern fishing technologies this situation changed = escalation in fishing intensity + leave fish no place to hide the twentieth century = The twentieth century
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "The twentieth century heralded an escalation in fishing intensity that is unprecedented in the history of the oceans, and modern fishing technologies leave fish no place to hide . Today, the only refuges from fishing are those we deliberately create."
explanation.step3: Hiểu câu hỏi: as _____ improved, this situation changed, and in the middle of the twentieth century => Đáp án là danh từ - một thứ mà khi cải thiện khiến tình thế thay đổi => Nhắc lại câu trước, 'this situation' ở đây là 'oceans were inaccessible' (chưa tiếp cận/đánh bắt được ở phần lớn đại dương) Áp dụng Linearthinking để nắm main idea: The twentieth century heralded an escalation in fishing intensity , and modern fishing technologies leave fish no place to hide. => Nếu bạn thấy 'heralded an escalation in fishing intensity' khó hiểu, ta hoàn toàn có thể dựa vào phần thông tin phía sau => Trước đây chưa tiếp cận được -> Có modern technologies -> Đánh bắt nhiều tới nỗi cá không có chỗ trốn => Công nghệ đánh bắt cải thiện khiến tình thế thay
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: F. fishing techniques

questions.prompt: However, as _____ improved, this situation changed, and in the middle of the twentieth century, policies were introduced to regulate _____.

explanation.step1: Question : and in the middle of the twentieth century, policies were introduced to regulate fish catches So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: policies = refuges from fishing were introduced = create
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Today, the only refuges from fishing are those we deliberately create ."
explanation.step3: Ở câu trước, ta biết công nghệ đã khiến tần suất fishing tăng nhanh, không kiểm soát được => Vậy theo như đề bài, thứ mà policies regulate (kiểm soát) chỉ có thể là việc đánh bắt cá => Ngoài ra, đọc thông tin trong bài cũng sẽ thấy Today , the only refuges from fishing are those (that) we deliberately create. => Những nơi trú ẩn khỏi việc đánh bắt - là nơi - chúng ta tự tạo ra => Tạo ra những vùng hạn chế đánh bắt cũng là một chính sách (policy) - trong việc kiểm soát fishing => So với list options -> Thấy đáp án phù hợp nhất là D - fish catches
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: D. fish catches

questions.prompt: These policies have not succeeded. Today, by comparison with _____ the oceans have very little legal protection.

explanation.step1: Question : These policies have not succeeded. Today, by comparison with the land the oceans have very little legal protection . So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: the land = the land have very little legal protection = trails far behind ... in terms of the area and the quality of protection given
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Unhappily, the sea trails far behind the land in terms of the area and the quality of protection given ."
explanation.step3: Ở câu trước ta đề cập tới các policies gồm có 'create refuge from fishing' - tuy nhiên đọc tiếp thì thấy 'Unhappily' => Biết là policy này không thành công - ứng với ' have not succeeded' => Biết cần đọc từ đó Áp dụng Linearthinking để nắm main idea: Unhappily , the sea trails far behind the land in terms of the area and the quality of protection given. => 'Trails' ở đây có nghĩa là đi lê, đi rất chậm -> 'Trails far behind' có thể hiểu là 'tụt lại phía sau' => Sea thì không bằng the land - về khía cạnh - the area and the quality of protection given => Sea được so sánh với the land -> Answer: I - the land
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: I. the land

questions.prompt: Despite the doubts that many officials have about the concept of _____, these should be at the heart of any action taken.

explanation.step1: Question : Despite the doubts that many officials have about the concept of marine reserves , these should be at the heart of any action taken . So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: marine reserve = Marine reserves be at the heart of any action taken = lie at the heart of the reform
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Marine reserves lie at the heart of the reform . But they will not be sufficient if they are implemented only here and there to shore up the crumbling edifice of the ‘rational fisheries management’ envisioned by scientists in the 1940s and 1950s. They have to be placed centre stage as a fundamental underpinning for everything we do in the oceans."
explanation.step3: Ở đầu đoạn 5 có thông tin 'To some people, creating marine reserves is an admission of failure ' => Một số người xem việc tạo ra marine reserves là sự chấp nhận thất bại => Điều này ứng với thông tin 'the doubts that many officials have about the concept of marine reserves' => Tới đây cũng có thể điền được đáp án là 'marine reserves' rồi, nhưng nếu chưa chắc ta đọc tiếp để tìm thông tin của vế sau Ở đoạn cuối cũng có nói ' Marine reserves lie at the heart of the reform .' => Ứng với thông tin ' these (marine reserves) should be at the heart of any action taken ' => Answer: marine reserves
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: H. marine reserves

questions.prompt: The consequences of further _____ are very serious, and may even affect our continuing existence.

explanation.step1: Question : The consequences of further failure are very serious, and may even affect our continuing existence . So sánh các cụm ở câu hỏi với bài đọc , ta có: failure = this cycle of failure affect our continuing existence = could have ramifications for human life itself
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "If we don’t break out of this cycle of failure , humanity will lose a key source of protein, and much more besides. Disrupting natural ecosystem processes, such as water purification, nutrient cycling, and carbon storage, could have ramifications for human life itself ."
explanation.step3: Áp dụng đọc connection Linearthinking để nắm main idea: 1 If we don’t break out of this cycle of failure , humanity will lose a key source of protein , and much more beside s . 2 Disrupting natural ecosystem processes , such as water purification, N2,N3 , could have ramifications for human life itself. => 1 + 2 : Nếu cứ tiếp tục thất bại - loài người - sẽ phải đối mặt với các hậu quả nghiệm trọng - mà đe dọa tới sự tồn tại của chúng ta => Nói cách khác, hậu quả của failure là rất nghiêm trọng => Answer: failure
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: C. failure

passages.title: Health Club Customer Research
content:
Example
Name:Answer
Selina ThompsonOccupation:[ _____ ]Age group:[ _____ ]Type of membership:[ _____ ]Length of membership:[ _____ ] yearsWhy joined:Recommended by a[ _____ ]Visits to club per month:Eight (on an average)Facility used most:[ _____ ]Facility not used (If any):Tennis courts (because reluctant to[ _____ ])Suggestions for improvements:Have more[ _____ ]Install [ _____ ] in the gym.Open [ _____ ] later at weekends.
transcript: [01:52] Man: Oh, excuse me, I wonder if you’d have the time to take part in some market research?
[01:57] Woman: Umm ... What’s it about?
[02:00] Man: About this club and your experiences and opinions about being a member. It’ll take less than five minutes.
[02:07] Woman: Oh ... OK then ... as long as it’s quick.
[02:11] Man: Can I start by taking your name?
[02:14] Woman: It’s Selina Thompson.
[02:16] Man: Is that T-H-O-M-P-S-O-N?
[02:21] Woman: Yes.
[02:22] Man: Great, thanks ... And what do you do for a living?
[02:27] Woman: Well, I’m an accountant but I’m between jobs at the moment.
[02:32] Man: I understand, but that’s the job I’ll put down on the form. And would you mind my asking which age group you fall into? Below thirty, thirty-one to fifty and above.
[02:46] Woman: Over fifty ... I think we can safely say.
[02:51] Man: Great, thanks. And which type of membership do you have?
[02:55] Woman: Sorry, I’m not sure what you mean? Do you mean how long ... ?
[02:59] Man: No, is it a single person membership ... ?
[03:02] Woman: Oh right ... no, it’s a family membership.
[03:05] Man: Thanks and how long have you been a member?
[03:09] Woman: Oh ... let me see ... I was certainly here five years ago ... and it was probably two to three years more than that ...
[03:19] Man: Shall I put down eight?
[03:21] Woman: I remember now ... it’s nine ... definitely ... sorry.
[03:24] Man: No problem ... I’ve got that. And the last question in this first part is, what brought you to the club?
[03:32] Woman: Sorry ... ?
[03:33] Man: How did you find out about the club? Did you see any ads?
[03:37] Woman: Well, I did actually but I have to say I wasn’t really attracted to the club because of that. It was through word of mouth.
[03:45] Man: So you were recommended by a friend?
[03:48] Woman: Actually my doctor ... I’d been suffering from high blood pressure and he said the club was very supportive of people with that condition, so I signed up.
[03:58] Man: Great ... thanks. Now for the second part of the form I want to ask a bit more about your experience of the club.
[04:37] Woman: Sure.
[04:38] Man: How often would you say you use the club ... ?
[04:42] Woman: It varies enormously depending on how busy I am.
[04:46] Man: Of course ... but on average ... per month?
[04:49] Woman: I’d say it averages out at twice a week.
[04:53] Man: OK, so eight on average.
[04:56] Woman: Yeah. And four of those are aqua-aerobics classes.
[05:00] Man: That leads me to the next question ... would you say the swimming pool is the facility you make most use of?
[05:07] Woman: Fair to say that ... yeah.
[05:09] Man: Right, thanks ... And are there any facilities you don’t use?
[05:14] Woman: One area I realise I’ve never used is the tennis courts ... and there’s one simple reason for that ...
[05:24] Man: You don’t play tennis?
[05:25] Woman: Actually, I’m not bad at it ... it’s that I’m not happy having to pay extra ... for that privilege.
[05:32] Man: I’ve made a note of that ... thanks. Now in the last section are there any suggestions or recommendations you have for improvements to the club?
[05:44] Woman: Only about health and fitness?
[05:47] Man: Anything at all ...
[05:48] Woman: Well, I’d like to see more social events ... it isn’t just a question of getting together for games or classes but other things, you know.
[05:59] Man: Yes, sure.
[06:00] Woman: And another thing that I was thinking when I had my yoga class in the gym last night - we were all sweltering in the heat - was that I think they should put in ... you know ...
[06:11] Man: Air conditioning.
[06:12] Woman: That’s exactly what I mean. The rooms are really light and well designed but they do need proper installations.
[06:20] Man: Sure ... well I’ve made a note of that ...
[06:23] Woman: Good.
[06:24] Man: ... so is there anything else you’d like to suggest ... about quality of service, for example?

[06:30] Woman: Oh, everyone’s very nice here ... they couldn’t be more friendly and helpful ... oh but I tell you what ... it’s a shame the restaurant isn’t open in the evening on Saturday ... and Sunday as well for that matter.
[06:44] Man: So ... the club should ...
[06:47] Woman: ... open it later on those days.
[06:49] Man: OK . well thank you very much, that’s all the questions .

passages.title: Outdoor Survival Skills
content: 📌 Making a steam pit
transcript: [00:50] AUDIO: Good morning everyone, and welcome to our outdoor survival programme. As you know, this week you’ll be learning some of the basic information and skills you need to look after yourself independently in the outdoors. These first two days we’ll be based here in the classroom, and then we’ll be taking a camping trip to put into practice some of the things you’ve learned. I’m going to start off with the topic of food. And to start with I’ll describe just two methods which we’ll be putting into practice at our camp, and which make use of natural resources: the steam pit and the bamboo pot. I’ve got two posters here to make things clearer ... And I’ll start with the steam pit here ...To make this you’ll need some dry sticks, some grass, some loose earth and some stones. And for this week only, some matches! The first thing you do is to dig a shallow pit in the place you’ve chosen to do your cooking. Let’s say about twenty five centimetres deep, and thirty centimetres wide. Your sticks have to be a bit wider than the pit, because you have to put a line of them along the top from one end of the pit to the other. Before setting light to these you take some large stones and arrange them on top. Then you start the fire and wait till the wooden platform burns through and the stones fall into the pit. At this point, brush away any pieces of hot ash from the stones - you can use a handful of grass - and then take another stick and push it down into the centre of the pit, between the stones.

[02:47] AUDIO: After that you cover the whole pit with a thick layer of grass. And then you can put your food on it. wrapped in more pieces of grass, like parcels. Finally, cover the whole thing with earth. You have to pat it firmly to seal the pit. Then all you have to do is take the stick out and pour a bit of water into the opening that it leaves. It should take about four hours for your food to cook, as it cooks slowly in the steam that’s created inside the pit. So ... simple but effective. The other method you’re going to practise this week is the bamboo oven. Now the steam pit is ideal in certain conditions because the heat is below ground level, for example, if there’s a strong wind and you’re afraid a fire might spread. But when it’s safe to have an open fire you can use the bamboo oven method. You get a length of bamboo, which as you probably know is hollow, and consists of a number of individual sections with a wall in-between. You use a sharp stick to make a hole in each of the dividing walls apart from the end one. Then you lean the bamboo over a fire, with the top propped up by a forked stick and the bottom sitting on the ground. You pour enough water in the top to fill the bottom section, and then light a fire underneath that section to heat the water. Then you put your food inside the top section, and the steam coming up the bamboo through the holes you made cooks it. I’m going to move on now, to food itself, and talk about some of the wild plants you might cook. I’m going to begin with fungi - that’s mushrooms and toadstools. I’m sure you’ll be aware that some of these are edible, and they’re delicious, but some of them are highly poisonous. Now whether they’re poisonous or not, all fungi that you find in the wild should be cooked before eating, because that helps to destroy any compounds in them that might be mildly toxic.

[05:36] AUDIO: But be aware that any amount of cooking won’t make poisonous varieties any safer to eat. Unless you can definitely identify a fungus you should never eat it. It’s not worth the risk. And you need to be really sure, because some fungi that are poisonous are very similar in appearance to certain edible varieties. They can easily be mistaken for each other. So ... having said all that, fungi are delicious when they’re freshly picked, and although they are only moderately nutritious, they do contain minerals which the body needs. I’ll move on now to leafy plants, which are generally ...

passages.title: Research Project On Attitudes Towards Study
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 3: "Research Project On Attitudes Towards Study"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [00:54] Tony: So how did you get on with your school-based research, Phoebe?
[00:58] Phoebe: Well, it was exhausting but really valuable.
[01:01] Tony: Good. What was the specific focus you chose?
[01:05] Phoebe: My title is ‘Attitudes towards study among eleven-twelve year-old pupils’.
[01:11] Tony: Right. And what made you choose that focus?

[01:14] Phoebe: Well, that’s a bit difficult ... lots of my classmates decided on their focus really early on.. .mainly on the basis of what they thought would help in their future career, you know, in their first year’s teaching.
[01:28] Tony: So that’s what helped you decide?
[01:31] Phoebe: Actually, it was that I came across a book written by experienced teachers on student attitudes and that motivated me to go for the topic.
[01:39] Tony: Okay. So what were your research questions or issues?
[01:44] Phoebe: Well I wanted to look at the ways students responded to different teachers particularly focusing on whether very strict teachers made teenagers less motivated.
[01:54] Tony: And, from your research, did you find that was true?
[01:57] Phoebe: No, not from what I saw you know, from my five days’ observation, talking to people and so forth.
[02:03] Tony: OK ... We’ll talk about the actual research methods in a moment, but before that, can you briefly summarise what your most striking findings are.

[02:13] Phoebe: Well, what really amazed me was the significant gender differences, I didn’t set out to focus on that but I found that boys were much more positive about being at school ... girls were more impatient, they talked a lot about wanting to grow up and leave school.
[02:30] Tony: Very interesting.
[02:31] Phoebe: Yeah ... it is. From doing the research it was clear to me that you might start out to focus on one thing but you pick up lots of unexpected insights.
[02:42] Tony: Right. Did you get any insights into teaching?

[02:45] Phoebe: Yes, certainly. I was doing a lot of observations of the way kids with very different abilities collaborate on certain tasks, you know, help each other and I began to realise that the lessons were developing in really unexpected ways.
[03:02] Tony: So what conclusion do you draw from that?
[03:05] Phoebe: Well, I know it’s necessary for teachers to prepare lessons carefully but it’s great if they also allow lessons to go their own ways.
[03:14] Tony: Good point. Now, I’m really pleased to see you doing this - analysing and drawing conclusions based on data.
[03:22] Phoebe: But surely this isn’t proper data ...
[03:25] Tony: Because it’s derived from such small-scale research? Well, as long as you don’t make grand claims for your findings, this data is entirely valid.
[03:34] Phoebe: Hmm .
[03:35] Tony: I like the way you’re already stepping back from the experience and thinking about what you’ve learned about research ... well done.
[03:42] Phoebe: But I know I could have done it better.
[03:44] Tony: As you become more experienced you’ll find ways to reduce the risk of difficulties.
[03:49] Phoebe: OK.
[04:20] Tony: So, let’s look in more detail at how you gathered your data. Let’s start with lesson observation.

[04:27] Phoebe: Well, it generally went quite smoothly. I chose my focus and designed my checklist. Then teachers allowed me into their classes without any problems, which surprised me. It was afterwards that the gruelling work started!
[04:42] Tony: Yeah, it’s very time consuming, isn’t it? Making sense of...analysing ... your observation notes.

[04:49] Phoebe: Absolutely. Much more so than interview data, for example ... that was relatively easy to process, though I wanted to make sure I used a high-quality recorder ... to make transcription easier and I had to wait until one became available.
[05:05] Tony: Right. And did you interview some kids as well?
[05:08] Phoebe: In the end, yes, I talked to ten, and they were great. I’d imagined I’d be bored listening to them, but.. .
[05:16] Tony: So it was easy to concentrate?

[05:19] Phoebe: Sure. One of the teachers was a bit worried about the ethics, you know, whether it was right to interview young pupils, and it took a while for him to agree to let me talk to three of the kids in his class but he relented in the end.
[05:33] Tony: Good. What other methods did you use?
[05:36] Phoebe: I experimented with questionnaires, but I really regret that now. I decided to share the work with another student but we had such different agendas it ended up taking twice as long.
[05:49] Tony: That’s a shame ... it might be worth you reflecting on ways you might improve on that for future projects.
[05:55] Phoebe: You’re right, yeah.
[05:56] Tony: OK.
[05:57] Phoebe: And the other thing I did was stills photography. I didn’t take as many pictures as I’d hoped to.
[06:04] Tony: Lack of time?
[06:06] Phoebe: It’s pretty easy just snapping away ... but I wanted each snap to have a purpose, you know, that would contribute to my research aims and I found that difficult.
[06:15] Tony: Well, that’s understandable, but remember...

passages.title: Saving The Juniper Plant
content: 📌 Saving the juniper plant
Background
Juniper was one of the first plants to colonise Britain after the last [ _____ ].
Its smoke is virtually [ _____ ], so juniper wood was used as fuel in illegal activities.
Oils from the plant were used to prevent [ _____ ]  spreading.
Nowadays, its berries are widely used to [ _____ ] food and drink.
Ecology
Juniper plants also support several species of insects and [ _____ ].
Problems
In current juniper populations, ratios of the [ _____ ] are poor.
Many of the bushes in each group are of the same age so [ _____ ] of whole populations is rapid.
Solutions
Plantlife is trialling novel techniques across [ _____ ] areas of England.
One measure is to introduce [ _____ ] for seedlings.
A further step is to plant [ _____ ] from healthy bushes.
transcript: [00:41] AUDIO: For my presentation, I’m going to summarise what I’ve found out about efforts to save one plant species ... the juniper bush. It once flourished in Britain and throughout the world’s temperate zones, but over the last few decades has declined considerably. Before I go on to explain the steps being taken to save it in England, let me start by looking at some background information and why the juniper has been so important in cultural as well as ecological terms, historically and in the present day. Firstly, I want to emphasise the fact that juniper is a very ancient plant. It has been discovered that it was actually amongst the first species of plants to establish itself in Britain in the period following the most recent Ice Age. And, as I say, it has a much valued place in British culture. It was used widely as a fuel during the Middle Ages because, when burnt, the smoke given off is all but invisible and so any illicit activities involving fire could go on without being detected, for example, cooking game hunted illegally. It also has valuable medicinal properties.

[01:56] AUDIO: Particularly during large epidemics, oils were extracted from the juniper wood and sprayed in the air to try to prevent the spread of infection in hospital wards. And these days, perhaps its most well known use is in cuisine...cooking, where its berries are a much-valued ingredient, used to flavour a variety of meat dishes and also drinks. Turning now to ecological issues, juniper bushes play an important role in supporting other living things. If juniper bushes are wiped out, this would radically affect many different insect and also fungus species. We simply cannot afford to let this species die out. So, why is the juniper plant declining at such a rapid rate? Well a survey conducted in the north and west of Britain in two thousand and four to five showed that a major problem is the fact that in present-day populations, ratios between the sexes are unbalanced and without a proper mix of male and female, bushes don’t get pollinated. Also, the survey found that in a lot of these populations, the plants are the same age, so this means that bushes grow old and start to die at similar times leading to swift extinction of whole populations.

[03:25] AUDIO: Now, the charity Plantlife is trying to do something to halt the decline in juniper species. It’s currently trying out two new major salvage techniques, this time focusing on lowland regions of England. The first thing it’s trying is to provide shelters for the seedlings in areas where juniper populations are fairly well established. These, of course, are designed to help protect the plants at their most vulnerable stage. A further measure is that in areas where colonies have all but died out, numbers are being bolstered by the planting of cuttings which have been taken from healthy bushes elsewhere. Now, I hope I’ve given a clear picture of the problems facing this culturally and ecologically valuable plant and of the measures being taken by Plantlife to tackle them. If anyone has any questions, I’d be happy to ...

explanation.step3: Đáp án cần điền là một danh từ Biết đáp án sắp tới khi nghe " Firstly " (chuẩn bị nói về ý đầu tiên) Nghe thấy "It was actually amongst the first species of plants to establish itself in Britain in the period following the most recent Ice Age" => Juniper là một trong những loại thực vật đầu tiên mọc ở Britain sau kỉ băng hà gần đây nhất (establish itself = colonize, following the most recent = after the last) => Đáp án: Ice Age
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: Ice Age

questions.prompt: Its smoke is virtually _____, so juniper wood was used as fuel in illegal activities.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "And, as I say, it has a much valued place in British culture. It was used widely as a fuel during the Middle Ages because, when burnt, the smoke given off is all but invisible and so any illicit activities involving fire could go on without being detected, for example, cooking game hunted illegally. It also has valuable medicinal properties."
explanation.step3: Mình cần nghe xem khói của juniper như thế nào mà nó được dùng trong illegal activities => Biết đáp án sắp tới khi nghe "it was used widely as fuel " (nói về công dụng) Nghe thấy "the smoke given off is all but invisible " (all but invisible = almost invisible) => Khi đốt thì gần như không có khói, khói không nhìn thấy được => Đáp án: invisible
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: invisible

questions.prompt: Oils from the plant were used to prevent _____  spreading.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Particularly during large epidemics, oils were extracted from the juniper wood and sprayed in the air to try to prevent the spread of infection in hospital wards. And these days, perhaps its most well known use is in cuisine...cooking, where its berries are a much-valued ingredient, used to flavour a variety of meat dishes and also drinks."
explanation.step3: Loại từ cần điền: noun + from , do đứng sau verb prevent có cấu trúc [prevent something from doing something] Mình cần nghe xem dầu từ juniper được dùng để ngăn chặn cái gì => Biết đáp án sắp tới khi nghe tới "... oils were extracted from the juniper wood. ..." Nghe thấy"... sprayed in the air to try to prevent the spread of infection => Bằng nghĩa với prevent infection from spreading => Đáp án: infection(s) from
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: infection from/infections from

questions.prompt: Nowadays, its berries are widely used to _____ food and drink.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Particularly during large epidemics, oils were extracted from the juniper wood and sprayed in the air to try to prevent the spread of infection in hospital wards. And these days, perhaps its most well known use is in cuisine...cooking, where its berries are a much-valued ingredient, used to flavour a variety of meat dishes and also drinks."
explanation.step3: Mình cần nghe xem quả juniper được dùng làm gì cho food and drinks => Biết đáp án sắp tới khi nghe "And these days, perhaps its most well known use is in cuisine " (đề cập tới ẩm thực) Nghe thấy "its berries are a much-valued ingredient, used to flavour a variety of meat dishes and also drinks " => Quả của cây được dùng để ướp thịt và làm hương vị cho thức uống => Đáp án: flavour
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: flavour

questions.prompt: Juniper plants also support several species of insects and _____.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Turning now to ecological issues, juniper bushes play an important role in supporting other living things. If juniper bushes are wiped out, this would radically affect many different insect and also fungus species. We simply cannot afford to let this species die out."
explanation.step3: Mình cần nghe xem juniper support cái gì, bên cạnh insects => Biết đáp án sắp tới khi nghe "Turning now to ecological issues" (liên quan tới ecology) Nghe thấy "if juniper bushes are wiped out, this would radically affect many different insect and also fungus species " => Nếu các bụi cây này bị xóa sổ, sẽ có ảnh hưởng lớn lên nhiều loại côn trùng và nấm => Bụi cây juniper support cho sự tồn tại của các loài này => Đáp án: fungus (species)
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: fungus species/fungus

questions.prompt: In current juniper populations, ratios of the _____ are poor.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "So, why is the juniper plant declining at such a rapid rate? Well a survey conducted in the north and west of Britain in two thousand and four to five showed that a major problem is the fact that in present-day populations, ratios between the sexes are unbalanced and without a proper mix of male and female, bushes don’t get pollinated."
explanation.step3: Mình cần nghe xem tỉ lệ của cái gì trong juniper population thì thấp => Biết đáp án sắp tới khi nghe "...a major problem is the fact that in present-day population..." Nghe thấy ratios between the sexes are unbalanced => Tỉ lệ giới tính của các cây bị thiếu cân bằng => Tỉ lệ thấp và không tốt => Đáp án: sexes
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: sexes

questions.prompt: Many of the bushes in each group are of the same age so _____ of whole populations is rapid.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Also, the survey found that in a lot of these populations, the plants are the same age, so this means that bushes grow old and start to die at similar times leading to swift extinction of whole populations."
explanation.step3: Mình cần nghe xem cái gì của population thì rapid => Biết đáp án sắp tới khi nghe " the plants are the same age " Nghe thấy "bushes grow old and start to die at similar times , leading to swift extinction of whole populations " => Dẫn đến sự tuyệt chủng của toàn bộ giống loài diễn ra nhanh hơn (swift = rapid) => Đáp án: extinction
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: extinction

questions.prompt: Plantlife is trialling novel techniques across _____ areas of England.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Now, the charity Plantlife is trying to do something to halt the decline in juniper species. It’s currently trying out two new major salvage techniques, this time focusing on lowland regions of England. The first thing it’s trying is to provide shelters for the seedlings in areas where juniper populations are fairly well established."
explanation.step3: Mình cần nghe xem Plantlife áp dụng phương pháp mới ở vùng nào của England => Biết đáp án sắp tới khi nghe "the charity Plantlife is trying to do something..." Nghe thấy "trying out two new major salvage techniques , this time focusing on lowland regions of England " (new = novel, region = area) => Đang thử hai phương pháp mới , tập trung vào các khu vực đồng bằng => Đáp án: lowland
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: lowland

questions.prompt: One measure is to introduce _____ for seedlings.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Now, the charity Plantlife is trying to do something to halt the decline in juniper species. It’s currently trying out two new major salvage techniques, this time focusing on lowland regions of England. The first thing it’s trying is to provide shelters for the seedlings in areas where juniper populations are fairly well established."
explanation.step3: Đáp án cần điền là introduce cái gì cho seedings => Biết đáp án sắp tới khi nghe "The first thing ...." (đang chuẩn bị nói về phương pháp đầu tiên) Nghe thấy provide shelters for the seedlings => Trong câu này provide có thể hiểu là introduce => Đáp án: shelter(s)
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: shelter/shelters

questions.prompt: A further step is to plant _____ from healthy bushes.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "These, of course, are designed to help protect the plants at their most vulnerable stage. A further measure is that in areas where colonies have all but died out, numbers are being bolstered by the planting of cuttings which have been taken from healthy bushes elsewhere."
explanation.step3: Mình cần nghe xem bước tiếp theo là trồng cái gì đó từ healthy bushes => Biết đáp án sắp tới khi nghe a further measure (chuẩn bị nhắc tới phương pháp tiếp theo) Nghe thấy "the planting of cuttings which have been taken from healthy bushes " => Việc trồng các cuttings được lấy từ các bụi cây khỏe mạnh => Đáp án: cuttings
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: cuttings

content: ExampleEnquiries about temporary workPersonal DetailsName:Jane[ _____ ]Address:[ _____ ] ExeterTelephone number:07792430921Availability:Can start work on[ _____ ]Work detailsPreferred type of work:Assistant[ _____ ]Relevant skills:Familiar with kitchen[ _____ ]Relevant qualifications:A[ _____ ] certificateTraining required:A[ _____ ] courseRefereeName:Dr Ruth PricePosition:[ _____ ]Phone number:[ _____ ]OtherApplicant has a form of [ _____ ]
transcript: [01:38] Man: Pinder’s Animal Park. Hello?
[01:45] Woman: Oh, hello, I’m ringing to ask whether you have any jobs available...
[01:50] Man: Ah, what sort of work are you looking for? Is that permanent, or part time or ...
[01:56] Woman: Actually I’m just looking for temporary work. I’m a student.
[02:01] Man: Oh right. I’ll just get a form, and ask you a few questions. Then I’ll pass your application on to our recruitment section. Is that OK?
[02:10] Woman: Fine, thank you.
[02:11] Man: So, starting with your name.
[02:14] Woman: It’s Jane Lamerton.
[02:16] Man: Is that L-A-double M-E-R-T-O-N?
[02:23] Woman: There’s only one M in it.
[02:25] Man: Oh, right. And your address?
[02:28] Woman: It’s forty-two West Lane.
[02:31] Man: Right ... And is that in Exeter?
[02:34] Woman: Yes.
[02:34] Man: Okay. And can you give me your mobile phone number?
[02:46] Man: Right. Now, the next thing is, when are you available to start work?
[02:52] Woman: I finish college on the eighth of June, that’s in three weeks’ time, but I can’t start work till the eleventh because I’ve got a hospital appointment on the tenth of June.

[03:04] Man: No problem. Now I need to ask you a few questions about the type of job that might be suitable. Do you have any particular kind of work in mind? It doesn’t necessarily mean that you will get work in the field that you want, but I can record your preferences.

[03:21] Woman: Well I’d do anything, and I have worked as an assistant animal keeper before, when I was still at school. But I’m studying at a catering college now, and I’d really like to get some experience as an assistant cook if possible.
[03:37] Man: Right. So that’s your first choice. Have you done that kind of job before?
[03:42] Woman: No. But I’ve helped my aunt sometimes - she runs a cafe in Exeter.
[03:48] Man: Mmm. Would you say you’ve got any relevant skills then?
[03:52] Woman: Well I’m used to using the kind of equipment you usually find in a kitchen.
[04:28] Man: OK . And I know you’re still studying, but do you already have any qualifications related to that kind of work? A hygiene qualification, for example?
[04:39] Woman: I haven’t, no, but I’ve got a certificate in food-handling. I did it before I decided to become a full-time student.

[04:47] Man: Fine. OK. That means you wouldn’t need any specific training if you did get the kind of work you wanted. But you’d have to do a short course on First Aid. All our new employees do that. It just takes half a day, and most people find it generally useful.
[05:06] Woman: Oh yes, I’m sure it is.
[05:08] Man: Well that’s about it, really. Just one last thing - can you give me the name of someone who would give you a reference? Like a previous employer or ...
[05:19] Woman: Oh yes, you can put Dr Ruth Price.
[05:23] Man: OK ... Is that one of your college lecturers?
[05:27] Woman: She’s my college tutor. She’s known me for over two years, and I’m sure she wouldn’t mind. In fact she’s given me a reference before.
[05:36] Man: Fine. We’d probably contact her by phone - do you happen to know her number?
[05:42] Woman: I’ve got it on my phone - yes - it’s 0208685114. That’s a landline.
[05:54] Man: Good. Well. As I say, I can’t promise anything, but I’ll pass your application on and you should hear in a few days. Is there anything else?
[06:04] Woman: Just one thing - I suffer from a particular type of colour blindness, and sometimes employers have to make special arrangements for that.
[06:14] Man: OK. I’ll make a note of that. It won’t be a problem, but it’s good that you’ve made us aware of it. You can provide us with more details if you are offered a job.
[06:24] Woman: Okay. Thanks very much. Bye.
[06:27] Man: Bye.

passages.title: Tamerton Centre
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 2: "Tamerton Centre"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [00:53] AUDIO: Hello everyone. I’ve been asked to talk to you this afternoon about next month’s trip to Tamerton Study Centre for the two-week course. Now some of the things I’m going say you may have already heard or read about ... but I think it’s important to emphasise a few key points. First of all, it’s worth reminding you why Tamerton was set up in the first place ... in the late nineteen sixties. That was really before all the concern with preserving the environment which everyone talks about these days. The idea was simply to get people out of the cities and into the country and to find out that just being outdoors can be very rewarding. This is not going to be a holiday in the usual sense. It’s called an adventure course because you’ll really be stretched to your limits but that in itself can be a positive thing. The group I took last year, for example, said that although they actually felt pretty weak and exhausted all the time, it really made them learn a lot about themselves and increased their confidence ... and in the end that’s the most important thing. Now all of you knew about policies at Tamerton before you signed up for it, so you know that in many ways it’s quite old fashioned - you don’t have a lot of choice in what you do. But something which I think makes the place so special is that you get to try so many different things, every day.

[02:33] AUDIO: For instance, one day you’ll do climbing and the next you’ll be surveying rock pools. It’s not intended that you become an expert in any of them ... it’s more like a taster, which you can follow up if you want. And there isn’t a lot of free time ... organised activities and talks, etc. go on until nine p.m. and lights go out at eleven p.m. There are table tennis tables, with all the equipment, and board games, though I have to say the pieces often go missing so it’s a good idea to take your own. There’s a DVD player with a good selection of films suitable for this age group so don’t take yours. Bed-time at eleven p.m. is strictly enforced ... and there’s a good reason for this. You’re all under eighteen and we organisers need to know that all group members are accounted for in the house as we close for the night. And of course you’ll be so exhausted anyway that you’ll be too sleepy to want to cause any trouble. Now, what should you pack? The information sheet tells you a lot about what clothing to bring ... but what about other things? Well, Tamerton House has its own small shop, but anything bigger is several miles away so you won’t have many opportunities for buying supplies.

[04:34] AUDIO: So in this last part of my talk, I’m going to explain what objects you should take with you to the Centre, what you can take if you want and also, very importantly, what you cannot take. Several of you came up to me before this talk and asked whether you can take things like kettles, or hairdryers. The answer is, there are plenty of Q16 these electrical appliances available in the Centre and they are of the proper voltage and are checked regularly. Yours may not be, so the rules at Tamerton say you can’t bring them into the Centre ... because it’s considered a fire risk ... remember it’s a very old house. Now, another question was about cell phones. Although you definitely can’t have them on during inside talks, you equally definitely need them when you’re out on exercises ... so they’re a must, I’m afraid. Anybody who wishes to talk to me about borrowing a phone for the fortnight, please see me after this talk. Now, the weather’s heating up at the moment and you’ll be outdoors a great deal. If you wear proper clothing, especially a hat, sun cream is optional. Also they sell high-factor cream in the shop so you don’t have to take any of your own, unless there’s a special kind you use.

[06:03] AUDIO: Now there’s a special note about things like deodorants which come in aerosol cans - I need to tell you that these are banned in the Centre because apparently they have the habit of setting off the fire alarms. If you want to take an aerosol can, you’ll actually be at risk of being told to leave. And finally, people having been asking about whether they need to take towels. Well, the Centre does provide one towel per guest, which you’re required to wash yourself. If you’re happy with that then don’t bring another. If not, take one of your own. Just remember how much outdoor exercise you’ll be doing ... and how dirty and wet you’ll be getting ...

passages.title: Preparations For Teaching Practice
content: 📌 Lesson Outline Year Three - Topic: Energy - Activities
transcript: [00:48] Tutor: Hello Eve, come in and sit down ... How’s it going?
[00:53] Eve: Fine thanks. I’m looking forward to my teaching practice next week.
[00:57] Tutor: Good. Now you’ve got two classes, haven’t you - Year 3 and Year 6. Have you done your lesson plans?

[01:04] Eve: Well, I’ve decided to take the topic of renewable energy ... I haven’t done a lesson plan for Year six yet, but I thought I’d base their lesson on an example of very simple technology. So I’ve brought this diagram to show you ... I got it from the Internet.
[01:22] Tutor: Let’s see ... A biogas plant ... So this is equipment for producing fuel from organic waste?
[01:30] Eve: Yes. The smaller container on the left is where you put the waste you’ve collected ...
[01:35] Tutor: Right, and from there it’s piped into the larger tank?
[01:40] Eve: That’s right. And that’s slurry on the base of the larger tank.
[01:46] Tutor: Right ... and what exactly is slurry?
[01:50] Eve: It’s a mixture of organic waste and water.
[01:53] Tutor: So is that pipe at the bottom where the water comes in?

[01:57] Eve: Yes it is ... As the slurry mixture digests it produces gas, and that rises to the top of the dome. Then when it’s needed it can be piped off for use as fuel in homes or factories. It’s very simple.
[02:11] Tutor: I suppose there’s some kind of safety valve to prevent pressure build-up?

[02:16] Eve: That’s the overflow tank. That container on the right. As the slurry expands some of it flows into that, and then once some of the gas has been piped off, the slurry level goes down again and the overflow tank empties again.
[02:32] Tutor: I see. Well I think that’s suitably simple for the age level it’s for. I look forward to seeing the whole lesson plan.
[02:39] Eve: Thanks. And can I show you my ideas for the Year three lesson?
[02:44] Tutor: Of course. Let’s look.

[03:24] Eve: I thought I’d introduce the topic by writing the word ‘energy’ on the board, and reinforcing the spelling and the pronunciation. Then I’ll do a little mime - you know, run on the spot or something - to convey the sense.
[03:38] Tutor: I’d keep it brief at this stage ...
[03:40] Eve: Yes, I will. Then I’ll wipe the word off and write the question ‘Where does energy come from?’, and see what the pupils come up with.
[03:50] Tutor: Fine. I’d suggest that you just brainstorm at this stage, and don’t reject any of their suggestions.

[03:56] Eve: Yes, that’s what I was going to do ... Then I’ve produced a set of simple statements, like ‘Energy makes cars move along the road’, and ‘Energy makes our bodies grow’. There are eight altogether.
[04:11] Tutor: Are you going to give them out as a handout? Or write them up on the board?

[04:15] Eve: First, I’ll put them on the board, and then I’ll read them out loud. And I’ll get the pupils to copy them out in their note books. I’ll also ask them to think up one more similar statement by themselves, and add it to the list.
[04:30] Tutor: Good idea.

[04:31] Eve: After that I thought I’d vary things a bit by sticking some pictures up ... of things like the sun and plants and food, and petrol, and a running child. And I’ll get the pupils to work out what order the pictures should come in, in terms of the energy chain.
[04:49] Tutor: I think that’s a very good idea. You could move the pictures around as the pupils give you directions.

[04:56] Eve: Yes, I think they’d enjoy that. And to finish off I’ve made a gap-fill exercise to give out. They’ll be doing that individually, and while they’re writing I’ll walk round and check their work.
[05:09] Tutor: Good ... And have you worked out the timing of all that? It’ll probably take you right through to the end of the.

passages.title: Creating Artificial Gills
content: 📌 Creating artificial gills
Background
Taking in oxygen: mammals - lungs; fish - gills
Long-held dreams - humans swimming underwater without oxygen tanks
Oxygen tanks considered too [ _____ ] and large
Attempts to extract oxygen directly from water
1960s - prediction that humans would have gills added by [ _____ ]
Ideas for artificial gills were inspired by research on fish gillsfish swim bladdersanimals without gills - especially bubbles used by [ _____ ]
Building a simple artificial gill
Make a watertight box of a materiaI which lets [ _____ ] pass through
Fill with air and submerge in water Important that the diver and the water keep[ _____ ]
The gill has to have a large[ _____ ]
Designers often use a network of small [ _____ ] on their gill
Main limitation - problems caused by increased [ _____ ]  in deeper water
Other applications
Supplying oxygen for use on [ _____ ]
Powering [ _____ ]  cells for driving machinery underwater
transcript: [00:50] AUDIO: In my talk today I’ll be exploring the idea of artificial gills. I’ll start by introducing the concept, giving some background and so forth and then I’ll go on to explain the technological applications, including a short, very simple, experiment I conducted. Starting with the background ... As everyone knows, all living creatures need oxygen to live. Mammals take in oxygen from the atmosphere by using their lungs, and fishes take oxygen from water by means of their gills, which of course in most fishes are located either side of their head. But human beings have always dreamt of being able to swim underwater like the fishes, breathing without the help of oxygen tanks. I don’t know whether any of you have done any scuba diving but it’s a real pain having to use all that equipment. You need special training, and it’s generally agreed that tanks are too heavy and big to enable most people to move and work comfortably underwater. So scientists are trying a different tack: rather than humans carrying an oxygen supply as they go underwater, wouldn’t it possible to extract oxygen in situ, that is, directly from the water, whilst swimming?

[02:15] AUDIO: In the nineteen sixties the famous underwater explorer Jacques Cousteau, for example, predicted that one day surgery could be used to equip humans with gills. He believed our lungs could be bypassed and we would learn to live underwater just as naturally as we live on land. But of course, most of us would prefer not to go to such extremes. I’ve been looking at some fairly simple technologies developed to extract oxygen from water - ways to produce a simple, practical artificial gill enabling humans to live and breathe in water without harm. Now, how scientists and inventors went about this was to look at the way different animals handled this - fairly obviously they looked at the way fishes breathe but also how they move down and float up to the surface using inflatable sacs, called swim bladders. Scientists also looked at animals without gills, which use bubbles of air underwater, notably beetles. These insects contrive to stay underwater for long periods by breathing from this bubble which they hold under their wing cases. By looking at these animal adaptations, inventors began to come up with their own ‘artificial gills’. Now making a crude gill is actually rather easy - more straightforward than you would think. You take a watertight box ... which is made of a material which is permeable to gas, that is, it allows it to pass through, inwards and outwards. You then fill this with air, fix it to the diver’s face and go down underwater.

[04:11] AUDIO: But a crucial factor is that the diver has to keep the water moving, so that water high in oxygen is always in contact with the gill, so he can’t really stay still. And to maximise this contact it’s necessary for your gill to have a big surface area. Different gill designers have addressed this problem in different ways but many choose to use a network or lattice-arrangement of tiny tubes as part of their artificial gills. Then the diver is able to breathe in and out - oxygen from the water passes through the outer walls of the gill and carbon-dioxide is expelled. In a nut-shell, that’s how the artificial gill works. So, having read about these simple gill mechanisms, I decided to create my own. I followed the procedure I’ve just described and it worked pretty well when I tried it out in the swimming pool ... I lasted underwater for nearly forty minutes! However, I’ve read about other people breathing through their gill for several hours. So the basic idea works well, but the real limitation is that these simple gills don’t work as the diver descends to any great depth because the pressure builds and a whole different set of problems are caused by that ... Research is being done into how these problems might be overcome . but that’s another story which has to be the subject of another talk!

[05:50] AUDIO: Despite this serious limitation, many people have high hopes for the artificial gill and they think it might have applications beyond simply enabling an individual to stay underwater for a length of time. For example, the same technology might be used to provide oxygen for submarines ... enabling them to stay submerged for months on end without resorting to potentially dangerous technologies such as nuclear power. Another idea is to use oxygen derived from the water as energy for fuel cells. These could power machinery underwater, such as robotic devices ... So, in my view, this is an area of technology with great potential. Now, if anyone has any questions, I’d be happy to answer ...

transcript: [02:04] Man: Hello, Brian Parks speaking.
[02:06] Woman: Oh hello, I’m calling about the advert in the paper ...
[02:09] Man: For the car?
[02:11] Woman: Er, yes, the Mini you’ve got advertised for sale.
[02:14] Man: Oh yes?
[02:15] Woman: I just wanted to find out a bit more information.
[02:19] Man: Of course, what would you like to know?
[02:21] Woman: It’s my brother who’s interested actually ... but he’s not in today so he asked me to call you.
[02:28] Woman: Great, thanks. So it’s a Mini ...
[02:32] Man: Yep.
[02:34] Woman: ... and how old is it?
[02:35] Man: Just coming up to thirteen years old.
[02:39] Woman: And I seem to remember from the ad that it’s grey?
[02:42] Man: That’s it ... doesn’t show the dirt!
[02:45] Woman: Absolutely ... anyway the colour shouldn’t be a problem for Jeff, you know, the important thing is the quality ...
[02:53] Man: Yes, of course.
[02:55] Woman: And what about mileage ... with it being pretty old it’s probably over a hundred thousand?
[03:01] Man: Actually it’s forty thousand less than that ... sixty-two thousand on the clock!
[03:06] Woman: Great! I remember now ... I’m confusing it with another ad I was looking at.
[03:11] Man: Right ... pleasant surprise then.

passages.title: The Treloar Valley Passenger Ferry
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 2: "The Treloar Valley Passenger Ferry"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [00:41] AUDIO: The valley and estuary of the River Treloar forms an unspoilt, beautiful landscape, rich in both wildlife and sites of historic interest. There are many ways to explore the area, and public transport links are good. It is possible to leave your car behind, and travel by boat, train or bus, with just short walks in-between stops. The Treloar Valley Passenger Ferry runs between villages along the river estuary, and provides a link with the train station at Berry, which is about ten minutes’ walk from the riverside village of Calton. In the past, the river was the main form of transport in the area, and as in the past, today’s ferry service operates according to nature. The river estuary is tidal, and so the ferry timetable differs from day to day, according to the times and height of the tide. The ferry is also seasonal, normally running between April and September, depending on the weather. A timetable for the whole year can be downloaded from the internet by visiting www dot treloarferry dot co dot uk. If you just want to sit and relax, and enjoy the lovely scenery, you can take a river cruise to Calton and back from the nearby city of Plymouth. In the past, steam ships brought early tourists along the same route - Queen Victoria and her family enjoyed such a trip in eighteen fifty six. The journey is quicker these days - the round trip takes between four and five hours, depending on tides and weather.

[02:30] AUDIO: f you prefer, you can travel upriver by boat and return to Plymouth by train. All cruise boats and trains have wheelchair access. For more information, and for departure times, ring Plymouth Boat Cruises on zero one seven, five two eight, two three one zero four. Trains run several times a day throughout the year between Calton and Plymouth, with various stops in-between. They are used by both local commuters and tourists who want to enjoy the beautiful scenery. The highlight of the journey is crossing the river on the stunning viaduct, which was built at the beginning of the twentieth century, and towers one hundred and twenty feet over the water. It is unnecessary to book, and tickets can be bought on the train. For information about fares and timetables, contact National Rail Enquiries by phone or online. The bus service in the Treloar Valley now connects all train stations and villages in the area. Specially for holiday makers, there’s a ‘Rover’ ticket which can be used at weekends and on national holidays, and allows unlimited journeys on those days. The Rover ticket provides great value for money, and is now even cheaper than it was last year. An adult ticket costs five pounds fifty a day, Senior Citizens can travel for four pounds fifty, and a family ticket for up to five people costs just twelve pounds. Tickets can be bought on the bus. At the centre of the Treloar Estuary area is the historic riverside village of Calton. The main road comes into the village from the south, and for those of you who are arriving by bus, it turns left just before the bridge and stops in the lay-by on the left hand side. From there it’s just a short walk to Calton’s various attractions.

[05:19] AUDIO: If you’re arriving by car, you have to leave it in the main car park. Go over the bridge and take the first turning on the right. Then go on until you come to the end of that road. It’s the only place to park in Calton but there’s no charge. If you’re interested in local history, there’s a museum in Calton with farming, fishing and household implements from the late nineteenth century. As you come in from the south, cross the river and go straight on the same road until you reach the end. Also on the subject of history, you can go and see the old mill which has recently been renovated and put back into use. Turn left before you come to the bridge. Then go straight on and then take the first turning on the right. This leads straight there. If you’re interested in arts and crafts, there’s a potter’s studio where you can watch the artist at work. After crossing the bridge turn left and it’s the second building on the left. Finally, when you feel in need of refreshments, there’s a cafe opposite the old boat house, and a picnic area near the mill.
